statements.name: Σ⁰₂ collection + Stable free set theorem for pairs

statements.label: \mathsf{B}\Sigma^0_2 + \mathsf{SIPT}^{2}_2
statements.name: Σ⁰₂ collection + Stable increasing polarized Ramsey theorem for pairs (2 colors)

statements.label: \mathsf{B}\Sigma^0_2 + \mathsf{SRT}^2_2
statements.name: Σ⁰₂ collection + Stable Ramsey's theorem for pairs

statements.label: \mathsf{B}\Sigma^0_3
statements.name: Σ⁰₃ collection
statements.definition: The collection (bounding) scheme for $\Sigma^0_3$ formulas.

statements.label: \mathsf{CADS} + \mathsf{PART}
statements.name: Cohesive ascending or descending sequence + Partition principle for ω+ω*

statements.label: \mathsf{CADS} + \mathsf{SADS}
statements.name: Cohesive ascending or descending sequence + Stable ascending or descending sequence

statements.label: \mathsf{CADS} + \mathsf{SCAC}
statements.name: Cohesive ascending or descending sequence + Stable chain–antichain principle

statements.label: \mathsf{CCAC}
statements.name: Cohesive chain–antichain principle
statements.definition: Every infinite partial order has an infinite stable suborder.
statements.instance: An infinite partial order.
statements.solution: An infinite stable suborder.

statements.label: \mathsf{COH} + \mathsf{EM} + \mathsf{GP}^{2}_2 + \mathsf{WKL}
statements.name: Cohesiveness principle + Erdős–Moser theorem + Grouping principle for pairs (2 colors) + Weak König's lemma

statements.label: \mathsf{COH} + \mathsf{EM} + \Pi^0_1\mathsf{G} + \mathsf{RRT}^{2}_2 + \mathsf{WKL}
statements.name: Cohesiveness principle + Erdős–Moser theorem + Π⁰₁ genericity + Rainbow Ramsey theorem for pairs (2 colors) + Weak König's lemma

statements.label: \mathsf{COH} + \mathsf{I}\Sigma^0_2 + \mathsf{WKL}
statements.name: Cohesiveness principle + Σ⁰₂ induction + Weak König's lemma

statements.label: \mathsf{COH} + \mathsf{SADS}
statements.name: Cohesiveness principle + Stable ascending or descending sequence

statements.label: \mathsf{COH} + \mathsf{SGP}^{2}_2
statements.name: Cohesiveness principle + Stable grouping principle for pairs (2 colors)

statements.label: \mathsf{COH} + \mathsf{SRT}^{2}_{<\infty}
statements.name: Cohesiveness principle + Stable Ramsey's theorem for pairs (finitely many colors)

statements.label: \mathsf{COH} + \mathsf{SRT}^2_2
statements.name: Cohesiveness principle + Stable Ramsey's theorem for pairs

statements.label: \mathsf{CRT}^{2}_2
statements.name: Cohesive Ramsey theorem for pairs (2 colors)
statements.definition: For every coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^2 \to 2$ there is an infinite set $H$ such that $f \restriction [H]^2$ is stable.
statements.instance: A coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^2 \to 2$.
statements.solution: An infinite set on which $f$ is stable.

statements.label: \mathsf{C}\Sigma
statements.name: Cardinality scheme
statements.definition: For every $n$, there is no $\Sigma^0_n$-definable injection from $\mathbb{N}$ into a finite set.

statements.label: \mathsf{C}\Sigma^0_2
statements.name: Σ⁰₂ cardinality scheme
statements.definition: There is no $\Sigma^0_2$-definable injection from $\mathbb{N}$ into a finite set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$.

statements.label: \mathsf{CTT}^{2}_2
statements.name: Cohesive tree theorem for pairs (2 colors)
statements.definition: For every coloring $f : [2^{<\mathbb{N}}]^2 \to 2$ of comparable pairs there is a set $H \subseteq 2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ on which $f$ is stable.
statements.instance: A coloring $f$ of the comparable pairs of $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ with 2 colors.
statements.solution: A set $H \subseteq 2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ on which $f$ is stable.

statements.label: \mathsf{CTT}^{2}_2 + \mathsf{STT}^{2}_2
statements.name: Cohesive tree theorem for pairs (2 colors) + Stable tree theorem for pairs (2 colors)

statements.label: \mathsf{D}^{2}_{<\infty}
statements.name: Δ⁰₂ subset principle for pairs (finitely many colors)
statements.definition: For every stable coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^2 \to k$ for every $k$, there is an infinite set $H$ and a color $i$ with $\lim_y f(x, y) = i$ for all $x \in H$.
statements.instance: A stable coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^2 \to k$.
statements.solution: An infinite limit-homogeneous set.

statements.label: \mathsf{D}_2\mathsf{IP}
statements.name: 2-disjointness intersection principle
statements.definition: Every nontrivial family of sets has a maximal subfamily with the $\mathsf{D}_2$ intersection property, i.e. in which any two distinct sets are disjoint. Equivalent to $\mathsf{ACA}_0$.
statements.instance: A nontrivial family of sets $\langle A_i : i \in \mathbb{N} \rangle$.
statements.solution: A maximal subfamily in which any two distinct sets are disjoint.

statements.label: \mathsf{DCT}'
statements.name: Dominated convergence theorem (variant)
statements.definition: Dominated convergence theorem, version with given limit: for $f, g$ and a sequence $(f_n)$ in $L^1$, if $(f_n)$ is dominated by $g$ and converges pointwise almost everywhere to $f$, then $\int f_n \to \int f$.

statements.label: 2\text{-}\mathsf{DNR}
statements.name: Existence of DNC functions relative to the jump (2-DNR)
statements.definition: For every $X$ there is a function $f$ with $f(e) \neq \Phi^{X'}_e(e)$ for every $e$.
statements.instance: A set $X$.
statements.solution: A function DNC relative to $X'$.
statements.caution: 2-DNR is DNC relative to the jump ∅′. It is not DNR₂ (or DNC₂), the problem of 2-valued DNC functions, which is strongly Weihrauch equivalent to [[wkl]] (Corollary 5.3 of [@brattkahendtlasskreuzer2017]).

statements.label: 2\text{-}\mathsf{DNR} + \mathsf{I}\Sigma^0_2
statements.name: Existence of DNC functions relative to the jump (2-DNR) + Σ⁰₂ induction

statements.label: \mathsf{D}^2_\omega
statements.name: Δ⁰₂ subset principle (variant)
statements.definition: The scheme asserting $\mathsf{D}^2_n$ for each $n$: for every $\Delta^0_n$-definable set $A$ there is an infinite set contained in $A$ or in its complement.

statements.label: \mathsf{ER}^1
statements.name: Erdős–Rado theorem for singletons (rationals)
statements.definition: For every $n$ and every coloring $f : \mathbb{Q} \to n$ there is a dense homogeneous set.
statements.instance: A number $n$ and a coloring $f : \mathbb{Q} \to n$.
statements.solution: A dense homogeneous set.

statements.label: \mathsf{ER}^{2}_2
statements.name: Erdős–Rado theorem for the rationals for pairs (2 colors)
statements.definition: For every coloring $f : [\mathbb{Q}]^2 \to 2$ there is either an infinite 0-homogeneous set or a 1-homogeneous set which is dense (equivalently, of order type η).
statements.instance: A coloring $f : [\mathbb{Q}]^2 \to 2$.
statements.solution: An infinite 0-homogeneous set or a 1-homogeneous set of order type $\eta$.

statements.label: \mathsf{FIP}
statements.name: Finite intersection principle
statements.definition: Every nontrivial family of sets has a maximal subfamily with the finite intersection property.
statements.instance: A nontrivial family of sets.
statements.solution: A maximal subfamily with the finite intersection property.

statements.label: \mathsf{FS}
statements.name: Free set theorem
statements.definition: Every function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^n \to \mathbb{N}$ has an infinite free set $H$: for every $s \in [H]^{n}$, if $f(s) \in H$ then $f(s) \in s$ for every exponent $n$.
statements.instance: A function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^n \to \mathbb{N}$.
statements.solution: An infinite free set.
statements.caution: FS names the free set theorem here. In papers on Hindman's theorem, FS(X) denotes the finite sums of X, and Hindman's theorem ([[ht]]) is also called the finite sums theorem.

statements.label: \mathsf{FS}^{2}
statements.name: Free set theorem for pairs
statements.definition: Every function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} \to \mathbb{N}$ has an infinite free set $H$: for every $s \in [H]^{2}$, if $f(s) \in H$ then $f(s) \in s$.
statements.instance: A function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} \to \mathbb{N}$.
statements.solution: An infinite free set.

statements.label: \mathsf{FS}^{3}
statements.name: Free set theorem for triples
statements.definition: Every function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{3} \to \mathbb{N}$ has an infinite free set $H$: for every $s \in [H]^{3}$, if $f(s) \in H$ then $f(s) \in s$.
statements.instance: A function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{3} \to \mathbb{N}$.
statements.solution: An infinite free set.

statements.label: G_\delta\text{-}\mathsf{REG}
statements.name: G_δ regularity
statements.definition: For every $G_\delta$ set $P \subseteq 2^\mathbb{N}$ there is an $F_\sigma$ set $Q \subseteq P$ with $\mu(Q) = \mu(P)$.
statements.instance: A (code for a) $G_\delta$ set $P \subseteq 2^\mathbb{N}$.
statements.solution: An $F_\sigma$ set $Q \subseteq P$ with $\mu(Q) = \mu(P)$.

statements.label: G_\delta\text{-}\mathsf{REG} + \mathsf{WWKL}
statements.name: G_δ regularity + Weak weak König's lemma

statements.label: 1\text{-}\mathsf{GEN}
statements.name: Existence of 1-generics (1-GEN)
statements.definition: For every $X$ there is a set which is Cohen 1-generic relative to $X$.
statements.instance: A set $X$.
statements.solution: A set 1-generic relative to $X$.

statements.label: 1\text{-}\mathsf{GEN} + 1\text{-}\mathsf{RAN} + \mathsf{WKL}
statements.name: Existence of 1-generics (1-GEN) + Existence of Martin-Löf randoms (1-RAN) + Weak König's lemma

statements.label: \mathsf{GP}^{2}_2
statements.name: Grouping principle for pairs (2 colors)
statements.definition: For every coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^2 \to 2$ and every largeness notion, there is an infinite sequence of large finite sets $F_0 < F_1 < \cdots$ and a color $i$ with $f(x, y) = i$ whenever $x \in F_a$, $y \in F_b$, $a < b$.
statements.instance: A coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^2 \to 2$ and a largeness notion.
statements.solution: An infinite sequence of large finite sets $F_0 < F_1 < \cdots$ grouping homogeneously.

statements.label: \mathsf{HYP}
statements.name: Hyperimmunity principle
statements.definition: For every $X$ there is a function not dominated by any $X$-computable function.
statements.instance: A set $X$.
statements.solution: A function which is hyperimmune relative to $X$.
statements.caution: HYP is the hyperimmunity problem here. In reverse mathematics, HYP usually denotes the ω-model of the hyperarithmetic sets (or HYP(X), the sets hyperarithmetic in X).

statements.label: \mathsf{IPT}
statements.name: Increasing polarized Ramsey theorem
statements.definition: For every coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^n \to k$ for every $k$, there are infinite sets $H_1, \dots, H_{n}$ such that $f$ is constant on all increasing tuples $x_1 < \dots < x_{n}$ with $x_i \in H_i$.
statements.instance: A coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^n \to k$.
statements.solution: An infinite increasing-homogeneous sequence of sets.

statements.label: \mathsf{IPT}^{2}_{<\infty}
statements.name: Increasing polarized Ramsey theorem for pairs (finitely many colors)
statements.definition: For every coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} \to k$ for every $k$, there are infinite sets $H_1, \dots, H_{2}$ such that $f$ is constant on all increasing tuples $x_1 < \dots < x_{2}$ with $x_i \in H_i$.
statements.instance: A coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} \to k$.
statements.solution: An infinite increasing-homogeneous sequence of sets.

statements.label: \mathsf{IPT}^{2}_2
statements.name: Increasing polarized Ramsey theorem for pairs (2 colors)
statements.definition: For every coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} \to 2$, there are infinite sets $H_1, \dots, H_{2}$ such that $f$ is constant on all increasing tuples $x_1 < \dots < x_{2}$ with $x_i \in H_i$.
statements.instance: A coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} \to 2$.
statements.solution: An infinite increasing-homogeneous sequence of sets.

statements.label: \mathsf{IPT}^{3}_{<\infty}
statements.name: Increasing polarized Ramsey theorem for triples (finitely many colors)
statements.definition: For every coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{3} \to k$ for every $k$, there are infinite sets $H_1, \dots, H_{3}$ such that $f$ is constant on all increasing tuples $x_1 < \dots < x_{3}$ with $x_i \in H_i$.
statements.instance: A coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{3} \to k$.
statements.solution: An infinite increasing-homogeneous sequence of sets.

statements.label: \mathsf{IPT}^{3}_2
statements.name: Increasing polarized Ramsey theorem for triples (2 colors)
statements.definition: For every coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{3} \to 2$, there are infinite sets $H_1, \dots, H_{3}$ such that $f$ is constant on all increasing tuples $x_1 < \dots < x_{3}$ with $x_i \in H_i$.
statements.instance: A coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{3} \to 2$.
statements.solution: An infinite increasing-homogeneous sequence of sets.

statements.label: \mathsf{IPTT}^{2}_{<\infty}
statements.name: Increasing polarized tree theorem for pairs (finitely many colors)
statements.definition: Polarized version of the tree theorem $\mathsf{TT}^{2}_{k}$: one asks for a sequence of subtrees isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$, one per coordinate, and only increasing chains are considered.
statements.instance: A coloring of the 2-element chains of $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$.
statements.solution: A sequence of 2 subtrees isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ which is homogeneous in the polarized sense.

statements.label: \mathsf{IPTT}^{2}_2
statements.name: Increasing polarized tree theorem for pairs (2 colors)
statements.definition: Polarized version of the tree theorem $\mathsf{TT}^{2}_{2}$: one asks for a sequence of subtrees isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$, one per coordinate, and only increasing chains are considered.
statements.instance: A coloring of the 2-element chains of $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$.
statements.solution: A sequence of 2 subtrees isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ which is homogeneous in the polarized sense.

statements.label: \mathsf{IPTT}^{3}_{<\infty}
statements.name: Increasing polarized tree theorem for triples (finitely many colors)
statements.definition: Polarized version of the tree theorem $\mathsf{TT}^{3}_{k}$: one asks for a sequence of subtrees isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$, one per coordinate, and only increasing chains are considered.
statements.instance: A coloring of the 3-element chains of $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$.
statements.solution: A sequence of 3 subtrees isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ which is homogeneous in the polarized sense.

statements.label: \mathsf{IPTT}^{3}_2
statements.name: Increasing polarized tree theorem for triples (2 colors)
statements.definition: Polarized version of the tree theorem $\mathsf{TT}^{3}_{2}$: one asks for a sequence of subtrees isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$, one per coordinate, and only increasing chains are considered.
statements.instance: A coloring of the 3-element chains of $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$.
statements.solution: A sequence of 3 subtrees isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ which is homogeneous in the polarized sense.

statements.label: \mathsf{I}\Sigma^0_2 + \mathsf{RT}^2_2
statements.name: Σ⁰₂ induction + Ramsey's theorem for pairs

statements.label: \mathsf{I}\Sigma^0_2 + \mathsf{RT}^2_2 + \mathsf{WKL}
statements.name: Σ⁰₂ induction + Ramsey's theorem for pairs + Weak König's lemma

statements.label: \mathsf{I}\Sigma^0_2 + \mathsf{STS}^{2}
statements.name: Σ⁰₂ induction + Stable thin set theorem for pairs

statements.label: \mathsf{I}\Sigma^0_3
statements.name: Σ⁰₃ induction
statements.definition: The induction scheme restricted to $\Sigma^0_3$ formulas.

statements.label: \mathsf{I}\Sigma^0_3 + \mathsf{RT}^{2}_{<\infty} + \mathsf{WKL}
statements.name: Σ⁰₃ induction + Ramsey's theorem for pairs (finitely many colors) + Weak König's lemma

statements.label: \mathsf{KL}
statements.name: König's lemma
statements.definition: Every infinite finitely branching subtree of $\mathbb{N}^{<\mathbb{N}}$ has an infinite path.
statements.instance: An infinite finitely branching tree.
statements.solution: An infinite path.

statements.label: \overline{\mathsf{D}}_2\mathsf{IP}
statements.name: 2 intersection principle
statements.definition: Every nontrivial family of sets has a maximal subfamily with the $\overline{\mathsf{D}}_2$ intersection property, i.e. in which any two distinct sets intersect. Called 2IP in Dzhafarov–Mummert 2022 (Definition 9.10.18).
statements.instance: A nontrivial family of sets $\langle A_i : i \in \mathbb{N} \rangle$.
statements.solution: A maximal subfamily in which any two distinct sets intersect.

statements.label: \mathsf{OPT}
statements.name: Omitting partial types
statements.definition: For every complete theory $T$ and every family of partial types, there is a model of $T$ omitting all the nonprincipal ones.
statements.instance: A complete theory $T$ and a family of partial types.
statements.solution: A model of $T$ omitting all the nonprincipal types of the family.

statements.label: \mathsf{P}^2_2
statements.name: Path principle
statements.definition: For any $\Pi^0_2$-definable sets $A_0, A_1$ with $A_0 \cup A_1 = \mathbb{N}$ there is an infinite set $H$ with $H \subseteq A_0$ or $H \subseteq A_1$.

statements.label: \mathsf{PA}
statements.name: Full first-order induction
statements.definition: The induction scheme for all arithmetical formulas.
statements.caution: Here PA is first-order Peano arithmetic (the full arithmetical induction scheme). In Weihrauch and computability papers, PA usually denotes the problem of finding a set of PA degree (Definition 6.2 of [@brattkahendtlasskreuzer2017]), entered here as [[padeg]].

statements.label: \mathsf{PART}
statements.name: Partition principle for ω+ω*
statements.definition: Every infinite linear order in which every element has finitely many predecessors or finitely many successors can be partitioned into its $\omega$ part and its $\omega^*$ part.
statements.instance: An infinite linear order in which every element has finitely many predecessors or finitely many successors.
statements.solution: The set of elements with finitely many predecessors.

statements.label: \mathsf{PHPM}
statements.name: Pigeonhole principle for measure
statements.definition: For every finite partition of $2^{\mathbb{N}}$ into Borel pieces, one piece has positive measure (formalized with codes; see Slaman).

statements.label: \Pi^0_1\mathsf{G}
statements.name: Π⁰₁ genericity
statements.definition: For every uniform sequence of dense $\Pi^0_1$ sets of strings, there is a set meeting each of them.
statements.instance: A uniform sequence of dense $\Pi^0_1$ sets of strings.
statements.solution: A set meeting every set of the sequence.

statements.label: \mathsf{POS}
statements.name: Positive-measure classes are inhabited
statements.definition: For every $G_\delta$ set $P \subseteq 2^\mathbb{N}$ with $\mu(P) > 0$ there is a closed set $F \subseteq P$ with $\mu(F) > 0$.
statements.instance: A (code for a) $G_\delta$ set $P \subseteq 2^\mathbb{N}$ with $\mu(P) > 0$.
statements.solution: A closed set $F \subseteq P$ with $\mu(F) > 0$.

statements.label: \mathsf{POS} + \mathsf{WWKL}
statements.name: Positive-measure classes are inhabited + Weak weak König's lemma

statements.label: \mathsf{POS}_1
statements.name: Positive-measure Π⁰₁ classes are inhabited
statements.definition: Every closed ($\Pi^0_1$) set of positive measure has an element (relativized to every set).
statements.instance: A closed set $P \subseteq 2^\mathbb{N}$ of positive measure.
statements.solution: An element of $P$.

statements.label: \mathsf{POS}_2
statements.name: Positive-measure Π⁰₂ classes are inhabited
statements.definition: Every $G_\delta$ subset of Cantor space with positive measure has an element (relativized to every set); equivalent to WWKL relative to the jump of any set.
statements.instance: A $G_\delta$ set $P \subseteq 2^\mathbb{N}$ of positive measure.
statements.solution: An element of $P$.

statements.label: \mathsf{ProdWQO}
statements.name: Products of wqos
statements.definition: The product of two well-quasi-orders is a well-quasi-order.

statements.label: \mathsf{ProdWQO} + \mathsf{WKL}
statements.name: Products of wqos + Weak König's lemma

statements.label: \mathsf{psRT}^{2}_2
statements.name: Pseudo Ramsey theorem for pairs (2 colors)
statements.definition: Every coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^2 \to 2$ has an infinite pseudo-homogeneous set $\{x_0 < x_1 < \dots\}$, i.e. one with $f(x_i, x_{i+1}) = f(x_j, x_{j+1})$ for all $i, j$.
statements.instance: A coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^2 \to 2$.
statements.solution: An infinite set $\{x_0 < x_1 < \dots\}$ with $f(x_i, x_{i+1}) = f(x_j, x_{j+1})$ for all $i, j$.

statements.label: \mathsf{PT}
statements.name: Polarized Ramsey theorem
statements.definition: For every coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^n \to k$ for every $k$, there are infinite sets $H_1, \dots, H_{n}$ such that $f$ is constant on all sets $\{x_1, \dots, x_{n}\} \in [\mathbb{N}]^n$ with $x_i \in H_i$.
statements.instance: A coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^n \to k$.
statements.solution: An infinite homogeneous sequence of sets $(H_1, \dots, H_n)$.

statements.label: \mathsf{PT}^{2}_{<\infty}
statements.name: Polarized Ramsey theorem for pairs (finitely many colors)
statements.definition: For every coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} \to k$ for every $k$, there are infinite sets $H_1, \dots, H_{2}$ such that $f$ is constant on all sets $\{x_1, \dots, x_{2}\} \in [\mathbb{N}]^{2}$ with $x_i \in H_i$.
statements.instance: A coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} \to k$.
statements.solution: An infinite homogeneous sequence of sets $(H_1, \dots, H_n)$.

statements.label: \mathsf{PT}^{2}_2
statements.name: Polarized Ramsey theorem for pairs (2 colors)
statements.definition: For every coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} \to 2$, there are infinite sets $H_1, \dots, H_{2}$ such that $f$ is constant on all sets $\{x_1, \dots, x_{2}\} \in [\mathbb{N}]^{2}$ with $x_i \in H_i$.
statements.instance: A coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} \to 2$.
statements.solution: An infinite homogeneous sequence of sets $(H_1, \dots, H_n)$.

statements.label: \mathsf{PT}^{3}_{<\infty}
statements.name: Polarized Ramsey theorem for triples (finitely many colors)
statements.definition: For every coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{3} \to k$ for every $k$, there are infinite sets $H_1, \dots, H_{3}$ such that $f$ is constant on all sets $\{x_1, \dots, x_{3}\} \in [\mathbb{N}]^{3}$ with $x_i \in H_i$.
statements.instance: A coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{3} \to k$.
statements.solution: An infinite homogeneous sequence of sets $(H_1, \dots, H_n)$.

statements.label: \mathsf{PT}^{3}_2
statements.name: Polarized Ramsey theorem for triples (2 colors)
statements.definition: For every coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{3} \to 2$, there are infinite sets $H_1, \dots, H_{3}$ such that $f$ is constant on all sets $\{x_1, \dots, x_{3}\} \in [\mathbb{N}]^{3}$ with $x_i \in H_i$.
statements.instance: A coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{3} \to 2$.
statements.solution: An infinite homogeneous sequence of sets $(H_1, \dots, H_n)$.

statements.label: \mathsf{PTT}^{2}_{<\infty}
statements.name: Polarized tree theorem for pairs (finitely many colors)
statements.definition: Polarized version of the tree theorem $\mathsf{TT}^{2}_{k}$: one asks for a sequence of subtrees isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$, one per coordinate.
statements.instance: A coloring of the 2-element chains of $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$.
statements.solution: A sequence of 2 subtrees isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ which is homogeneous in the polarized sense.
statements.caution: PTT names the polarized tree theorem of Dzhafarov, Hirst and Lakins [@dzhafarovhirstlakins2010] here. Kihara, Marcone and Pauly [@kiharamarconepauly2020] use PTT₁ and PTT₂ for the one-sided and two-sided perfect tree theorems ([[perfect1]], [[perfect2]]).

statements.label: \mathsf{PTT}^{2}_2
statements.name: Polarized tree theorem for pairs (2 colors)
statements.definition: Polarized version of the tree theorem $\mathsf{TT}^{2}_{2}$: one asks for a sequence of subtrees isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$, one per coordinate.
statements.instance: A coloring of the 2-element chains of $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$.
statements.solution: A sequence of 2 subtrees isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ which is homogeneous in the polarized sense.
statements.caution: PTT names the polarized tree theorem of Dzhafarov, Hirst and Lakins [@dzhafarovhirstlakins2010] here. PTT₂ without a superscript is the two-sided perfect tree theorem of Kihara, Marcone and Pauly ([[perfect2]]).

statements.label: \mathsf{PTT}^{3}_{<\infty}
statements.name: Polarized tree theorem for triples (finitely many colors)
statements.definition: Polarized version of the tree theorem $\mathsf{TT}^{3}_{k}$: one asks for a sequence of subtrees isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$, one per coordinate.
statements.instance: A coloring of the 3-element chains of $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$.
statements.solution: A sequence of 3 subtrees isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ which is homogeneous in the polarized sense.

statements.label: \mathsf{PTT}^{3}_2
statements.name: Polarized tree theorem for triples (2 colors)
statements.definition: Polarized version of the tree theorem $\mathsf{TT}^{3}_{2}$: one asks for a sequence of subtrees isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$, one per coordinate.
statements.instance: A coloring of the 3-element chains of $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$.
statements.solution: A sequence of 3 subtrees isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ which is homogeneous in the polarized sense.

statements.label: 1\text{-}\mathsf{RAN}
statements.name: Existence of Martin-Löf randoms (1-RAN)
statements.definition: For every $X$ there is a set which is Martin-Löf random relative to $X$.
statements.instance: A set $X$.
statements.solution: A set Martin-Löf random relative to $X$.

statements.label: 2\text{-}\mathsf{RAN}
statements.name: Existence of 2-randoms (2-RAN)
statements.definition: For every $X$ there is a set which is 2-random relative to $X$.
statements.instance: A set $X$.
statements.solution: A set 2-random relative to $X$.

statements.label: \mathsf{RCOLOR}_2
statements.name: Ramsey-type 2-coloring
statements.definition: For every infinite locally 2-colorable graph $G = (V, E)$ there is an infinite $H \subseteq V$ such that every finite $V_0 \subseteq V$ induces a subgraph with a 2-coloring giving color 0 to every vertex of $V_0 \cap H$.
statements.instance: An infinite locally 2-colorable graph $G = (V, E)$.
statements.solution: An infinite $H \subseteq V$ such that every finite $V_0 \subseteq V$ induces a subgraph with a 2-coloring giving color 0 to $V_0 \cap H$.

statements.label: \mathsf{RCOLOR}_3
statements.name: Ramsey-type 3-coloring
statements.definition: For every infinite locally 3-colorable graph $G = (V, E)$ there is an infinite $H \subseteq V$ such that every finite $V_0 \subseteq V$ induces a subgraph with a 3-coloring giving color 0 to every vertex of $V_0 \cap H$.
statements.instance: An infinite locally 3-colorable graph $G = (V, E)$.
statements.solution: An infinite $H \subseteq V$ such that every finite $V_0 \subseteq V$ induces a subgraph with a 3-coloring giving color 0 to $V_0 \cap H$.

statements.label: \mathsf{RRT}
statements.name: Rainbow Ramsey theorem
statements.definition: Every k-bounded function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^n \to \mathbb{N}$ (each color used at most k times) has an infinite rainbow set $H$, i.e. $f$ is injective on $[H]^{n}$ for every exponent $n$.
statements.instance: A k-bounded function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^n \to \mathbb{N}$.
statements.solution: An infinite rainbow set.

statements.label: \mathsf{RRT}^{2}_2
statements.name: Rainbow Ramsey theorem for pairs (2 colors)
statements.definition: Every 2-bounded function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} \to \mathbb{N}$ (each color used at most 2 times) has an infinite rainbow set $H$, i.e. $f$ is injective on $[H]^{2}$.
statements.instance: A 2-bounded function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} \to \mathbb{N}$.
statements.solution: An infinite rainbow set.
statements.context: The rainbow Ramsey theorem: every coloring of pairs in which each color is used at most twice has an infinite set on which the coloring is injective. It follows from RT²₂; Csima and Mileti [@csimamileti2009] showed that it is strictly weaker and not implied by COH. It follows from the Erdős–Moser theorem [@kang2014].

statements.label: \mathsf{RRT}^{3}_2
statements.name: Rainbow Ramsey theorem for triples (2 colors)
statements.definition: Every 2-bounded function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{3} \to \mathbb{N}$ (each color used at most 2 times) has an infinite rainbow set $H$, i.e. $f$ is injective on $[H]^{3}$.
statements.instance: A 2-bounded function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{3} \to \mathbb{N}$.
statements.solution: An infinite rainbow set.

statements.label: \mathsf{RRT}^{3}_2 + \mathsf{RT}^2_2 + \mathsf{WKL}
statements.name: Rainbow Ramsey theorem for triples (2 colors) + Ramsey's theorem for pairs + Weak König's lemma

statements.label: \mathsf{RRT}^{4}_2
statements.name: Rainbow Ramsey theorem for 4-tuples (2 colors)
statements.definition: Every 2-bounded function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{4} \to \mathbb{N}$ (each color used at most 2 times) has an infinite rainbow set $H$, i.e. $f$ is injective on $[H]^{4}$.
statements.instance: A 2-bounded function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{4} \to \mathbb{N}$.
statements.solution: An infinite rainbow set.

statements.label: \mathsf{RSAT}
statements.name: Ramsey-type satisfiability
statements.definition: For every finitely satisfiable set $C$ of propositional formulas with infinitely many atoms, there is an infinite set $H$ of atoms that is homogeneous for $C$: some truth value can be given to all atoms of $H$ consistently with every finite subset of $C$.
statements.instance: A finitely satisfiable set $C$ of propositional formulas with infinitely many atoms.
statements.solution: An infinite set of atoms homogeneous for $C$.

statements.label: \mathsf{RT}
statements.name: Ramsey's theorem
statements.definition: Every coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^n \to k$ has an infinite homogeneous set for every exponent $n$ for every $k$.
statements.instance: A coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^n \to k$.
statements.solution: An infinite set $H$ such that $f$ is constant on $[H]^{n}$.

statements.label: \mathsf{RT}^{2}_{<\infty}
statements.name: Ramsey's theorem for pairs (finitely many colors)
statements.definition: Every coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} \to k$ has an infinite homogeneous set for every $k$.
statements.instance: A coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} \to k$.
statements.solution: An infinite set $H$ such that $f$ is constant on $[H]^{2}$.

statements.label: \mathsf{RT}^2_2 + \mathsf{WKL}
statements.name: Ramsey's theorem for pairs + Weak König's lemma

statements.label: \mathsf{RT}^{3}_{<\infty}
statements.name: Ramsey's theorem for triples (finitely many colors)
statements.definition: Every coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{3} \to k$ has an infinite homogeneous set for every $k$.
statements.instance: A coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{3} \to k$.
statements.solution: An infinite set $H$ such that $f$ is constant on $[H]^{3}$.

statements.label: \mathsf{RWKL}
statements.name: Ramsey-type weak König's lemma
statements.definition: For every infinite binary tree $T$ there is an infinite set $H$ which is homogeneous for a path through $T$.
statements.instance: An infinite binary tree $T$.
statements.solution: An infinite set $H$ such that some path of $T$ is constant on $H$.

statements.label: \mathsf{RWKL}_2
statements.name: Ramsey-type WKL (variant RWKL₂)
statements.definition: Flood's $\mathsf{RKL}(1)$: for every infinite set of strings $\Sigma$ there is an infinite set homogeneous for a path through the tree $T_\Sigma$ generated by $\Sigma$ (so for $\Pi^0_2$-definable trees).
statements.instance: An infinite set of strings $\Sigma$.
statements.solution: An infinite set homogeneous for a path through the tree $T_\Sigma$ generated by $\Sigma$.

statements.label: \mathsf{RWKL}_\omega
statements.name: Ramsey-type WKL (variant RWKL_ω)
statements.definition: Flood's $\mathsf{RKL}(<\omega)$: the scheme asserting, for each arithmetical formula defining a tree with arbitrarily long strings, that there is an infinite set homogeneous for a path through it.

statements.label: \mathsf{RWWKL}
statements.name: Ramsey-type weak weak König's lemma
statements.definition: RWKL restricted to trees of positive measure.
statements.instance: A binary tree of positive measure.
statements.solution: An infinite set homogeneous for a path through the tree.

statements.label: \mathsf{RWWKL}_2
statements.name: Ramsey-type WWKL (variant)
statements.definition: $2\text{-}\mathsf{RWWKL}$: for every $X$ and every $X'$-computable subtree of $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ with positive measure there is an infinite set homogeneous for it.
statements.instance: A set $X$ and an $X'$-computable tree $T \subseteq 2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ of positive measure.
statements.solution: An infinite set homogeneous for a path through $T$.

statements.label: \mathsf{SADS} + \mathsf{SEM}
statements.name: Stable ascending or descending sequence + Stable Erdős–Moser theorem

statements.label: \mathsf{SADS} + \mathsf{SGP}^{2}_2 + \mathsf{WKL}
statements.name: Stable ascending or descending sequence + Stable grouping principle for pairs (2 colors) + Weak König's lemma

statements.label: \mathsf{SEM}
statements.name: Stable Erdős–Moser theorem
statements.definition: EM restricted to stable tournaments.
statements.instance: An infinite stable tournament.
statements.solution: An infinite transitive subtournament.

statements.label: \mathsf{SER}^{2}_2
statements.name: Stable Erdős–Rado theorem for pairs (2 colors)
statements.definition: For every stable coloring $f : [\mathbb{Q}]^2 \to 2$ there is either an infinite homogeneous set of color 0 or a homogeneous set of color 1 of order type η.
statements.instance: A stable coloring $f : [\mathbb{Q}]^2 \to 2$.
statements.solution: An infinite 0-homogeneous set or a 1-homogeneous set of order type $\eta$.

statements.label: \mathsf{SFS}^{2}
statements.name: Stable free set theorem for pairs
statements.definition: Every stable function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} \to \mathbb{N}$ has an infinite free set $H$: for every $s \in [H]^{2}$, if $f(s) \in H$ then $f(s) \in s$.
statements.instance: A stable function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} \to \mathbb{N}$.
statements.solution: An infinite free set.

statements.label: \mathsf{SFS}^{3}
statements.name: Stable free set theorem for triples
statements.definition: Every stable function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{3} \to \mathbb{N}$ has an infinite free set $H$: for every $s \in [H]^{3}$, if $f(s) \in H$ then $f(s) \in s$.
statements.instance: A stable function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{3} \to \mathbb{N}$.
statements.solution: An infinite free set.

statements.label: \mathsf{SGP}^{2}_2
statements.name: Stable grouping principle for pairs (2 colors)
statements.definition: For every stable coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^2 \to 2$ and every largeness notion, there is an infinite sequence of large finite sets $F_0 < F_1 < \cdots$ and a color $i$ with $f(x, y) = i$ whenever $x \in F_a$, $y \in F_b$, $a < b$.
statements.instance: A stable coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^2 \to 2$ and a largeness notion.
statements.solution: An infinite sequence of large finite sets $F_0 < F_1 < \cdots$ grouping homogeneously.

statements.label: \mathsf{SIPT}^{2}_{<\infty}
statements.name: Stable increasing polarized Ramsey theorem for pairs (finitely many colors)
statements.definition: For every stable coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} \to k$ for every $k$, there are infinite sets $H_1, \dots, H_{2}$ such that $f$ is constant on all increasing tuples $x_1 < \dots < x_{2}$ with $x_i \in H_i$.
statements.instance: A stable coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} \to k$.
statements.solution: An infinite increasing-homogeneous sequence of sets.

statements.label: \mathsf{SIPT}^{2}_2
statements.name: Stable increasing polarized Ramsey theorem for pairs (2 colors)
statements.definition: For every stable coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} \to 2$, there are infinite sets $H_1, \dots, H_{2}$ such that $f$ is constant on all increasing tuples $x_1 < \dots < x_{2}$ with $x_i \in H_i$.
statements.instance: A stable coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} \to 2$.
statements.solution: An infinite increasing-homogeneous sequence of sets.

statements.label: \mathsf{SIPTT}^{2}_{<\infty}
statements.name: Stable increasing polarized tree theorem for pairs (finitely many colors)
statements.definition: Polarized version of the tree theorem $\mathsf{TT}^{2}_{k}$: one asks for a sequence of subtrees isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$, one per coordinate, and only increasing chains are considered; restricted to stable colorings.
statements.instance: A coloring of the 2-element chains of $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$.
statements.solution: A sequence of 2 subtrees isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ which is homogeneous in the polarized sense.

statements.label: \mathsf{SIPTT}^{2}_2
statements.name: Stable increasing polarized tree theorem for pairs (2 colors)
statements.definition: Polarized version of the tree theorem $\mathsf{TT}^{2}_{2}$: one asks for a sequence of subtrees isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$, one per coordinate, and only increasing chains are considered; restricted to stable colorings.
statements.instance: A coloring of the 2-element chains of $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$.
statements.solution: A sequence of 2 subtrees isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ which is homogeneous in the polarized sense.

statements.label: \mathsf{SPT}^{2}_{<\infty}
statements.name: Stable polarized Ramsey theorem for pairs (finitely many colors)
statements.definition: For every stable coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} \to k$ for every $k$, there are infinite sets $H_1, \dots, H_{2}$ such that $f$ is constant on all sets $\{x_1, \dots, x_{2}\} \in [\mathbb{N}]^{2}$ with $x_i \in H_i$.
statements.instance: A stable coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} \to k$.
statements.solution: An infinite homogeneous sequence of sets $(H_1, \dots, H_n)$.

statements.label: \mathsf{SPT}^{2}_2
statements.name: Stable polarized Ramsey theorem for pairs (2 colors)
statements.definition: For every stable coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} \to 2$, there are infinite sets $H_1, \dots, H_{2}$ such that $f$ is constant on all sets $\{x_1, \dots, x_{2}\} \in [\mathbb{N}]^{2}$ with $x_i \in H_i$.
statements.instance: A stable coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} \to 2$.
statements.solution: An infinite homogeneous sequence of sets $(H_1, \dots, H_n)$.

statements.label: \mathsf{SPTT}^{2}_{<\infty}
statements.name: Stable polarized tree theorem for pairs (finitely many colors)
statements.definition: Polarized version of the tree theorem $\mathsf{TT}^{2}_{k}$: one asks for a sequence of subtrees isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$, one per coordinate; restricted to stable colorings.
statements.instance: A coloring of the 2-element chains of $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$.
statements.solution: A sequence of 2 subtrees isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ which is homogeneous in the polarized sense.

statements.label: \mathsf{SPTT}^{2}_2
statements.name: Stable polarized tree theorem for pairs (2 colors)
statements.definition: Polarized version of the tree theorem $\mathsf{TT}^{2}_{2}$: one asks for a sequence of subtrees isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$, one per coordinate; restricted to stable colorings.
statements.instance: A coloring of the 2-element chains of $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$.
statements.solution: A sequence of 2 subtrees isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ which is homogeneous in the polarized sense.

statements.label: \mathsf{SRAM}
statements.name: Stable Ramsey for measure
statements.definition: For every set $X$ there is a set $Y$ such that every stable coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^2 \to 2$ with $f \le_T X$ has an infinite homogeneous set $H \le_T Y$.

statements.label: \mathsf{SRRT}^{2}_2
statements.name: Stable rainbow Ramsey theorem for pairs (2 colors)
statements.definition:
Every rainbow-stable 2-bounded coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} 	o \mathbb{N}$ has an infinite rainbow, that is a set $H$ on which $f$ is injective. $f$ is rainbow-stable if for every $x$, either there is $y 
eq x$ with $f(x, s) = f(y, s)$ for almost every $s$, or $f(x, s) 
eq f(y, s)$ for every $y 
eq x$ and almost every $s$.
statements.instance: A rainbow-stable 2-bounded coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} \to \mathbb{N}$.
statements.solution: An infinite rainbow.

statements.label: \mathsf{SRRT}^{3}_2
statements.name: Stable rainbow Ramsey theorem for triples (2 colors)
statements.definition: The stable rainbow Ramsey theorem for triples: $\mathsf{RRT}^3_2$ restricted to 2-bounded colorings of triples that are rainbow-stable, as for pairs in Definition 1.5 of Patey (2015). The paper uses it in Corollary 5.26 without defining stability for triples.
statements.instance: A rainbow-stable 2-bounded function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{3} \to \mathbb{N}$.
statements.solution: An infinite rainbow set.

statements.label: \mathsf{SRT}^{2}_{<\infty}
statements.name: Stable Ramsey's theorem for pairs (finitely many colors)
statements.definition: Every stable coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^2 \to k$ has an infinite homogeneous set for every $k$. $f : [\mathbb{N}]^2 \to k$ is stable if $\lim_y f(x, y)$ exists for every $x$.
statements.instance: A stable coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^2 \to k$.
statements.solution: An infinite homogeneous set.

statements.label: \mathsf{StCADS}
statements.name: Stable CADS
statements.definition: Every infinite linear order has a suborder that is of type ω, of type ω*, or strongly of type ω + ω*.
statements.instance: An infinite linear order $L$.
statements.solution: A suborder of $L$ of type $\omega$, of type $\omega^*$, or strongly of type $\omega + \omega^*$.

statements.label: \mathsf{StCOH}
statements.name: Stable cohesiveness
statements.definition: COH restricted to stable sequences $\vec R$ (for each $n$, $n \in R_i$ for almost all $i$ or for almost no $i$).
statements.instance: A stable sequence of sets $\vec R$.
statements.solution: An infinite $\vec R$-cohesive set.

statements.label: \mathsf{StCRT}^{2}_2
statements.name: Cohesive Ramsey theorem for stable-like colorings for pairs (2 colors)
statements.definition: For every coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^2 \to 2$ there is an infinite set $S$ on which $f$ is strongly stable: $(\forall n)(\exists y)(\forall x \in S)(x < n \to (\forall z \in S)[z > y \to f(x,y) = f(x,z)])$.
statements.instance: A coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^2 \to 2$.
statements.solution: An infinite set on which $f$ is strongly stable.

statements.label: \mathsf{STS}^{2}
statements.name: Stable thin set theorem for pairs
statements.definition: Every stable function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} \to \mathbb{N}$ has an infinite thin set $H$, i.e. $f[[H]^{2}] \neq \mathbb{N}$.
statements.instance: A stable function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} \to \mathbb{N}$.
statements.solution: An infinite set $H$ with $f[[H]^{2}] \neq \mathbb{N}$.

statements.label: \mathsf{STS}^{3}
statements.name: Stable thin set theorem for triples
statements.definition: Every stable function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{3} \to \mathbb{N}$ has an infinite thin set $H$, i.e. $f[[H]^{3}] \neq \mathbb{N}$.
statements.instance: A stable function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{3} \to \mathbb{N}$.
statements.solution: An infinite set $H$ with $f[[H]^{3}] \neq \mathbb{N}$.

statements.label: \mathsf{STT}^{2}_{<\infty}
statements.name: Stable tree theorem for pairs (finitely many colors)
statements.definition: For every stable coloring $f$ of the $2$-element chains of $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ with k colors for every $k$, there is a subtree $S \subseteq 2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ on whose chains $f$ is constant.
statements.instance: A stable coloring of $[2^{<\mathbb{N}}]^{2}$ with k colors.
statements.solution: A homogeneous subtree isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$.

statements.label: \mathsf{STT}^{2}_2
statements.name: Stable tree theorem for pairs (2 colors)
statements.definition: For every stable coloring $f$ of the $2$-element chains of $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ with 2 colors, there is a subtree $S \subseteq 2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ on whose chains $f$ is constant.
statements.instance: A stable coloring of $[2^{<\mathbb{N}}]^{2}$ with 2 colors.
statements.solution: A homogeneous subtree isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$.

statements.label: \mathsf{TS}^{2}
statements.name: Thin set theorem for pairs
statements.definition: Every function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} \to \mathbb{N}$ has an infinite thin set $H$, i.e. $f[[H]^{2}] \neq \mathbb{N}$.
statements.instance: A function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} \to \mathbb{N}$.
statements.solution: An infinite set $H$ with $f[[H]^{2}] \neq \mathbb{N}$.

statements.label: \mathsf{TS}^{3}
statements.name: Thin set theorem for triples
statements.definition: Every function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{3} \to \mathbb{N}$ has an infinite thin set $H$, i.e. $f[[H]^{3}] \neq \mathbb{N}$.
statements.instance: A function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{3} \to \mathbb{N}$.
statements.solution: An infinite set $H$ with $f[[H]^{3}] \neq \mathbb{N}$.

statements.label: \mathsf{TT}^1_{<\infty}
statements.name: Tree theorem for singletons
statements.definition: For every $k$, every coloring $f : 2^{<\mathbb{N}} \to k$ has a homogeneous subtree isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$.
statements.instance: A number $k$ and a coloring $f : 2^{<\mathbb{N}} \to k$.
statements.solution: A homogeneous subtree isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$.

statements.label: \mathsf{TT}^1_2
statements.name: Tree theorem for singletons (2 colors)
statements.definition: Every coloring $f : 2^{<\mathbb{N}} \to 2$ has a homogeneous subtree isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$.
statements.instance: A coloring $f : 2^{<\mathbb{N}} \to 2$.
statements.solution: A homogeneous subtree isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$.

statements.label: \mathsf{TT}^{2}_{<\infty}
statements.name: Tree theorem for pairs (finitely many colors)
statements.definition: For every coloring $f$ of the $2$-element chains of $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ with k colors for every $k$, there is a subtree $S \subseteq 2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ on whose chains $f$ is constant.
statements.instance: A coloring of $[2^{<\mathbb{N}}]^{2}$ with k colors.
statements.solution: A homogeneous subtree isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$.

statements.label: \mathsf{TT}^{2}_2
statements.name: Tree theorem for pairs (2 colors)
statements.definition: For every coloring $f$ of the $2$-element chains of $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ with 2 colors, there is a subtree $S \subseteq 2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ on whose chains $f$ is constant.
statements.instance: A coloring of $[2^{<\mathbb{N}}]^{2}$ with 2 colors.
statements.solution: A homogeneous subtree isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$.

statements.label: \mathsf{TT}^{3}_2
statements.name: Tree theorem for triples (2 colors)
statements.definition: For every coloring $f$ of the $3$-element chains of $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ with 2 colors, there is a subtree $S \subseteq 2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ on whose chains $f$ is constant.
statements.instance: A coloring of $[2^{<\mathbb{N}}]^{3}$ with 2 colors.
statements.solution: A homogeneous subtree isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$.

statements.label: \mathsf{WSCAC}
statements.name: Weakly stable chain–antichain principle
statements.definition: Every infinite weakly stable partial order has an infinite chain or antichain; a poset is weakly stable if every element is below almost all elements, above almost all elements, or incomparable with almost all elements.
statements.instance: An infinite weakly stable partial order.
statements.solution: An infinite chain or antichain.

statements.label: \mathsf{WSRRT}^{2}_2
statements.name: Weakly stable rainbow Ramsey theorem for pairs (2 colors)
statements.definition: Every weakly stable 2-bounded function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} \to \mathbb{N}$ (each color used at most 2 times) has an infinite rainbow set $H$, i.e. $f$ is injective on $[H]^{2}$.
statements.instance: A weakly stable 2-bounded function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} \to \mathbb{N}$.
statements.solution: An infinite rainbow set.

statements.label: 2\text{-}\mathsf{WWKL}
statements.name: 2-Weak weak König's lemma
statements.definition: WWKL relativized to the jump: every $\Delta^0_2$-tree of positive measure has a path.
statements.instance: A $\Delta^0_2$ binary tree of positive measure.
statements.solution: A path through it.

statements.caution: The acronyms HB and HBT name the Heine–Borel covering lemma in some papers and the Hahn–Banach theorem ([[hb]]) in others: check the definition in each paper.
statements.label: \textsf{Heine–Borel}_{[0,1]}
statements.name: Heine–Borel covering lemma for [0,1]
statements.definition: Every covering of the closed unit interval $[0,1]$ by a sequence of open intervals has a finite subcovering.

statements.label: \textsf{Bounded König’s lemma}
statements.name: Bounded König's lemma
statements.definition: Every infinite tree $T \subseteq \mathbb{N}^{<\mathbb{N}}$ bounded by a function $g$ (that is, $\sigma(j) < g(j)$ for all $\sigma \in T$ and $j < |\sigma|$) has an infinite path.

statements.label: \textsf{Unif. cont.}_{[0,1]}
statements.name: Uniform continuity on [0,1]
statements.definition: Every continuous function on the closed interval $[0,1]$ is uniformly continuous.

statements.label: \textsf{Bounded}_{[0,1]}
statements.name: Boundedness of continuous functions on [0,1]
statements.definition: Every continuous function on the closed interval $[0,1]$ is bounded.

statements.label: \textsf{Weierstrass}
statements.name: Weierstrass approximation theorem
statements.definition: For every continuous function $\varphi$ on $[0,1]$ there is a polynomial $f$ with $|\varphi(x) - f(x)| < 1$ for all $x \in [0,1]$ (equivalently, a sequence of polynomials converging to $\varphi$ at rate $2^{-n}$).

statements.label: \textsf{Riemann}
statements.name: Riemann integrability of continuous functions
statements.definition: For every continuous function $\varphi$ on a closed bounded interval $[a,b]$, the Riemann integral $\int_a^b \varphi(x)\,dx$ exists and is finite.

statements.label: \textsf{Completeness}
statements.name: Gödel's completeness theorem
statements.definition: Every countable consistent set of sentences has a countable model. Equivalent over RCA₀ to Lindenbaum's lemma, to the compactness theorem, and to the completeness and compactness theorems for propositional logic (Theorem IV.3.3).

statements.label: \textsf{Formally real}
statements.name: Orderability of formally real fields
statements.definition: Every countable formally real field is orderable (equivalently, has a real closure).

statements.label: \textsf{Unique alg. closure}
statements.name: Uniqueness of algebraic closures
statements.definition: Every countable field has a unique algebraic closure, up to isomorphism over the field.

statements.label: \textsf{Prime ideal}
statements.name: Existence of prime ideals
statements.definition: Every countable commutative ring contains a prime ideal (equivalently, a radical ideal).

statements.label: \textsf{Brouwer}
statements.name: Brouwer fixed point theorem
statements.definition: If $C$ is the convex hull of a nonempty finite set of points of $\mathbb{R}^n$, every continuous $f : C \to C$ has a fixed point. Already the case of the unit square is equivalent to $\mathsf{WKL}_0$.

statements.label: \textsf{Peano}
statements.name: Peano existence theorem
statements.definition: If $f(x, y)$ is continuous in a neighborhood of $(0, 0)$, the initial value problem $y' = f(x, y)$, $y(0) = 0$ has a continuously differentiable solution in some interval containing $0$.

statements.label: \textsf{Banach sep.}
statements.name: Banach separation theorem
statements.definition: Two disjoint open convex sets in a separable Banach space can be strictly separated by a bounded linear functional.

statements.label: \textsf{Range existence}
statements.name: Range existence
statements.definition: Every one-to-one function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ has a range. Equivalent over RCA₀ to $\Sigma^0_1$ comprehension.

statements.label: \textsf{Cauchy}_{\mathbb{R}}
statements.name: Cauchy completeness of the reals
statements.definition: Every Cauchy sequence of real numbers converges.

statements.label: \textsf{Seq. compactness}
statements.name: Sequential compactness of compact metric spaces
statements.definition: In any compact metric space, every sequence of points has a convergent subsequence.

statements.label: \textsf{Ascoli}
statements.name: Ascoli lemma
statements.definition: Every bounded equicontinuous sequence of continuous functions between compact metric spaces has a uniformly convergent subsequence.

statements.label: \textsf{Strong alg. closure}
statements.name: Existence of strong algebraic closures
statements.definition: Every countable field has a strong algebraic closure, that is, an algebraic closure whose embedding has a range (equivalently, every countable field is isomorphic to a subfield of a countable algebraically closed field).

statements.label: \textsf{Vector space basis}
statements.name: Bases of countable vector spaces
statements.definition: Every countable vector space over a countable field has a basis (already over $\mathbb{Q}$, Theorem III.4.3(3)).

statements.label: \textsf{Transcendence base}
statements.name: Existence of transcendence bases
statements.definition: For every pair of countable fields $K \subseteq L$ there is a transcendence base for $L$ over $K$.

statements.label: \textsf{Maximal ideal}
statements.name: Existence of maximal ideals
statements.definition: Every countable commutative ring has a maximal ideal (already every countable integral domain, Theorem III.5.5(3)).

statements.label: \textsf{Torsion}
statements.name: Existence of torsion subgroups
statements.definition: Every countable Abelian group has a subgroup consisting of its torsion elements.

statements.label: \textsf{Radó}
statements.name: Radó selection lemma
statements.definition: Countable Radó selection lemma (strong version): given a sequence of partial functions $f_i$ from $\mathbb{N}$ to $\mathbb{N}$ such that every finite set is included in some $\mathrm{dom}(f_i)$ and the values at each point are bounded, there is $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ each of whose finite restrictions agrees with some $f_i$ (with the uniformity condition of Theorem III.7.8).

statements.caution: As a sentence, Σ¹₁ separation is equivalent to ATR₀, and the weaker Π¹₁ separation lies strictly between Δ¹₁-CA₀ and ATR₀. As Weihrauch problems the order is reversed: Σ¹₁-Sep is strongly Weihrauch equivalent to [[ucnn]] (Theorem 3.11 of [@kiharamarconepauly2020]) and lies strictly below Π¹₁-Sep ([[pi11-sep-w]]).
statements.label: \Sigma^1_1\text{-}\mathsf{SEP}
statements.name: Σ¹₁ separation
statements.definition: For any $\Sigma^1_1$ formulas $\varphi_0(n)$, $\varphi_1(n)$ with no $n$ satisfying both, there is a set $Z$ containing every $n$ with $\varphi_1(n)$ and no $n$ with $\varphi_0(n)$.

statements.caution: As a sentence, CWO is equivalent to ATR₀ over RCA₀; the Weihrauch problem CWO of Kihara, Marcone and Pauly is strongly Weihrauch equivalent to [[ucnn]] (Theorem 5.5 of [@kiharamarconepauly2020]). The two-sided version is [[cwo2]].
statements.label: \mathsf{CWO}
statements.name: Comparability of countable well-orderings
statements.definition: For any two countable well-orderings, one embeds as an initial segment of the other: $\forall X \forall Y ((\mathrm{WO}(X) \wedge \mathrm{WO}(Y)) \to (|X| \le |Y| \vee |Y| \le |X|))$.

statements.label: \Sigma^1_1\textsf{ bounding}
statements.name: Σ¹₁ bounding
statements.definition: If every element of an analytic set (given by an analytic code) is a well-ordering, there is a well-ordering $Y$ bounding the order types of all of them.

statements.label: \textsf{Ulm}
statements.name: Existence of Ulm resolutions
statements.definition: Every countable reduced Abelian $p$-group has an Ulm resolution.

statements.label: \Sigma^0_1\text{-}\mathsf{Det}
statements.name: Open determinacy
statements.definition: Every game on $\mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$ with a $\Sigma^0_1$ payoff set is determined.

statements.label: \Delta^0_1\text{-}\mathsf{Det}
statements.name: Clopen determinacy
statements.definition: Every game on $\mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$ with a $\Delta^0_1$ payoff set is determined.

statements.label: \textsf{Cantor–Bendixson}
statements.name: Cantor–Bendixson theorem (perfect kernels)
statements.definition: Every tree $T \subseteq \mathbb{N}^{<\mathbb{N}}$ has a perfect kernel (equivalently, a perfect subtree $P$ such that only countably many paths of $T$ are not paths of $P$).

statements.label: \textsf{Silver}
statements.name: Silver's theorem
statements.definition: Every coanalytic equivalence relation on $\mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$ has either countably many equivalence classes or a perfect set of pairwise inequivalent points (already for $\Delta^0_2$ relations).

statements.label: \textsf{Div+Red}
statements.name: Divisible–reduced decomposition
statements.definition: Every countable Abelian group is the direct sum of a divisible group and a reduced group.

statements.label: (\Sigma^0_1 \wedge \Pi^0_1)\text{-}\mathsf{Det}
statements.name: Determinacy of differences of open sets
statements.definition: Every game on $\mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$ whose payoff set is the intersection of a $\Sigma^0_1$ and a $\Pi^0_1$ set is determined.

statements.label: \Delta^0_2\text{-}\mathsf{RT}_{\infty}
statements.name: Δ⁰₂ Ramsey theorem (infinite exponent)
statements.definition: For every $\Delta^0_2$ set $P \subseteq [\mathbb{N}]^\mathbb{N}$ there is an infinite $H$ such that $[H]^\mathbb{N} \subseteq P$ or $[H]^\mathbb{N} \cap P = \emptyset$ (equivalently, the same for arithmetical $P$).

statements.label: \textsf{CA}_\mu
statements.name: Countable additivity of Borel measures
statements.definition: For any compact metric space $X$ and any Borel measure $\mu$ on $X$, $\mu$ is countably additive (equivalently, any covering of $[0,1]$ by open intervals $(a_n, b_n)$ has $\sum_n |a_n - b_n| \ge 1$).

statements.label: \textsf{Vitali}
statements.name: Vitali covering theorem
statements.definition: If $I$ Vitali covers an interval $E$, then $I$ contains a pairwise disjoint sequence of intervals $I_n$ such that $\mu(E \setminus \bigcup_n I_n) = 0$.

statements.label: \textsf{MCT}_\mu
statements.name: Monotone convergence theorem (measures)
statements.definition: The monotone convergence theorem for Borel measures on compact metric spaces (already for Lebesgue measure on $[0,1]$).

statements.label: \mathsf{WO}(\omega^\omega)
statements.name: Well-orderedness of ω^ω
statements.definition: The ordinal $\omega^\omega$ (in its standard notation) is well ordered. Not provable in $\mathsf{WKL}_0$: $\omega^\omega$ is the proof-theoretic ordinal of $\mathsf{RCA}_0$ and $\mathsf{WKL}_0$.

statements.label: \textsf{Dickson's lemma}
statements.name: Dickson's lemma
statements.definition: For each $m \in \mathbb{N}$, the $m$-fold Cartesian power $\mathbb{N}^m$ is well quasiordered.

statements.label: \textsf{Hilbert basis theorem}
statements.name: Hilbert basis theorem
statements.definition: For every countable field $K$ and every $m \in \mathbb{N}$, every ideal of the polynomial ring $K[x_1, \dots, x_m]$ is finitely generated (already for $K = \mathbb{Q}$).

statements.label: \textsf{Higman's theorem}
statements.name: Higman's theorem
statements.definition: If $Q$ is a well quasiordering, then so is $Q^{<\mathbb{N}}$, the finite sequences of elements of $Q$ quasiordered by embedding: $\langle a_i : i < m \rangle \leq \langle b_j : j < n \rangle$ if there are $j_0 < \dots < j_{m-1} < n$ with $a_i \leq b_{j_i}$.

statements.label: \textsf{Hall's theorem}_{\mathrm{lf}}
statements.name: Hall's theorem for countable locally finite bipartite graphs
statements.definition: A countable locally finite bipartite graph has a perfect matching if and only if it satisfies the Hall condition.

statements.label: \textsf{Marriage theorem}
statements.name: Marriage theorem for countable regular bipartite graphs
statements.definition: Every countable bipartite graph which is $n$-regular for some $n \geq 1$ has a perfect matching (equivalently, already for $n = 2$).

statements.label: \textsf{Podewski–Steffens}
statements.name: Podewski–Steffens theorem (König coverings)
statements.definition: Every countable bipartite graph has a König covering: a pair $(C, M)$ where $C$ is a vertex covering, $M$ a matching, and $C$ consists of exactly one vertex from each edge of $M$.

statements.label: \textsf{Weak-* closure}
statements.name: Smallest weak-*-closed set containing a countable set
statements.definition: For every separable Banach space $X$ and countable set $Y \subseteq X^*$, there is a smallest weak-*-closed set in $X^*$ containing $Y$ (equivalently, a smallest weak-*-closed convex set, or linear subspace).

statements.label: \textsf{Lub}
statements.name: Least upper bound principle
statements.definition: Every bounded sequence of real numbers has a least upper bound.

statements.label: \textsf{MCT}
statements.name: Monotone convergence theorem
statements.definition: Every bounded increasing sequence of real numbers is convergent.
statements.instance: A bounded increasing sequence $(x_n)$ of real numbers.
statements.solution: Its limit $\sup_n x_n$.

statements.label: \textsf{Max}_{[0,1]}
statements.name: Maximum principle
statements.definition: Every continuous real-valued function on $[0,1]$ has a supremum, and attains it.

statements.label: \textsf{Perfect set}
statements.name: Perfect set theorem
statements.definition: Every uncountable analytic set (in particular every uncountable closed set) has a nonempty perfect subset.

refs.loc: Theorem I.11.5(3); Theorems V.4.3 and V.5.5

statements.label: \textsf{Lusin}
statements.name: Lusin's separation theorem
statements.definition: Any two disjoint analytic sets can be separated by a Borel set.

refs.loc: Theorem I.11.5(4); Sections V.3 and V.5

statements.label: \textsf{Baire}
statements.name: Baire category theorem
statements.definition: In a complete separable metric space, the intersection of a sequence of dense open sets is dense.

statements.label: \textsf{Ulm}_{\cong}
statements.name: Ulm's theorem (isomorphism form)
statements.definition: Any two countable reduced Abelian $p$-groups which have the same Ulm invariants are isomorphic.

statements.label: \mathsf{LLPO}
statements.name: Lesser limited principle of omniscience
statements.definition: Given $p \in 2^{\mathbb{N}}$ with at most one $1$, find $i \in \{0, 1\}$ such that $p(2n + i) = 0$ for all $n$. Equivalently (Weihrauch), choice from a nonempty co-c.e. subset of $\{0, 1\}$ ($\mathsf{C}_2$).
statements.instance: A sequence $p \in 2^{\mathbb{N}}$ with at most one $1$.
statements.solution: A parity $i$ such that $p$ is zero on all positions of parity $i$.
statements.context: The lesser limited principle of omniscience comes from constructive mathematics. As a problem, it asks, given two binary sequences at most one of which contains a 1, for one of them which contains only zeros; it is Weihrauch-equivalent to choice on {0, 1}. Its parallelization is WKL [@brattkagherardi2011], and it lies below the intermediate value theorem.

statements.label: \mathsf{LPO}
statements.name: Limited principle of omniscience
statements.definition: Given $p \in 2^{\mathbb{N}}$, decide whether $p$ is the constant zero sequence.
statements.instance: A sequence $p \in 2^{\mathbb{N}}$.
statements.solution: $1$ if $p = 0^\omega$, and $0$ otherwise.
statements.context: The limited principle of omniscience asks whether a given binary sequence contains a 1. It is the prototype of a discontinuous problem in the Weihrauch lattice [@weihrauch1992b] [@brattkagherardi2011]; its parallelization is equivalent to lim.

statements.label: \mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}}
statements.name: Closed choice on the natural numbers
statements.definition: Given an enumeration of the complement of a nonempty set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$, find an element of $A$. The problems Weihrauch below it are those computable with finitely many mind changes.
statements.instance: An enumeration of $\mathbb{N} \setminus A$ for some nonempty $A$.
statements.solution: An element of $A$.
statements.context: Closed choice on ℕ: given an enumeration of the complement of a non-empty set of natural numbers, find an element of it. Problems Weihrauch-reducible to C_ℕ are exactly those computable with finitely many mind changes [@brattkadebrechtpauly2012]. It lies strictly between LPO and lim [@brattkagherardi2011b] [@neumannpauly2018].

statements.label: \lim
statements.name: Limit operation
statements.definition: Given a convergent sequence $(p_n)$ in $\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$, find its limit.
statements.instance: A convergent sequence $(p_n)_n$ in Baire space.
statements.solution: $\lim_n p_n$.
statements.context: The limit operation on Baire space is Weihrauch-equivalent to the Turing jump and to the parallelization of LPO [@brattkagherardi2011]; problems reducible to it are the limit computable ones. Its compositional products give the analogues of the arithmetical hierarchy in the Weihrauch lattice; for instance, the Bolzano–Weierstrass theorem is the jump of WKL [@brattkagherardimarcone2012].

statements.label: \mathsf{IVT}
statements.name: Intermediate value theorem
statements.definition: Every continuous $f : [0, 1] \to \mathbb{R}$ with $f(0) \cdot f(1) < 0$ has a zero. Weihrauch equivalent to connected choice on $[0, 1]$.
statements.instance: A continuous $f : [0,1] \to \mathbb{R}$ with $f(0) \cdot f(1) < 0$.
statements.solution: A real $x \in [0,1]$ with $f(x) = 0$.

statements.label: \mathsf{BWT}_{\mathbb{R}}
statements.name: Bolzano–Weierstrass theorem
statements.definition: Every bounded sequence of real numbers has a cluster point.
statements.instance: A bounded sequence of reals.
statements.solution: A cluster point of the sequence.

statements.label: \mathsf{WKL}'
statements.name: Jump of weak König's lemma
statements.definition: The jump of $\mathsf{WKL}$: given a sequence converging to (a code of) an infinite binary tree, find a path through the limit tree.
statements.instance: A convergent sequence of codes for an infinite binary tree $T$.
statements.solution: An infinite path through $T$.

statements.label: \mathsf{WKL}''
statements.name: Double jump of weak König's lemma
statements.definition: The jump of $\mathsf{WKL}'$.
statements.instance: A double limit of codes for an infinite binary tree $T$.
statements.solution: An infinite path through $T$.

statements.label: \mathsf{DS}
statements.name: Descending sequences in ill-founded orders
statements.definition: Every ill-founded linear order has an infinite descending sequence.
statements.instance: An ill-founded linear order.
statements.solution: An infinite descending sequence.

statements.label: \mathsf{BS}
statements.name: Bad sequences in non-wqos
statements.definition: Every quasi-order which is not a well-quasi-order has an infinite bad sequence.
statements.instance: A quasi-order which is not a wqo.
statements.solution: An infinite bad sequence.

statements.label: \mathsf{K}_{\mathbb{N}}
statements.name: Compact choice on the natural numbers
statements.definition: Given a bound $b$ and an enumeration of the complement of a nonempty set $A \subseteq \{0, \dots, b\}$, find an element of $A$. Strongly Weihrauch equivalent to the finite parallelization $\mathsf{C}_2^*$ of LLPO.
statements.instance: A bound $b$ and an enumeration of the complement of a nonempty $A \subseteq \{0, \dots, b\}$.
statements.solution: An element of $A$.

statements.caution: C_ℝ, sometimes written CR, is closed choice on the reals. In randomness papers CR abbreviates computable randomness ([[cran]]).
statements.label: \mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{R}}
statements.name: Closed choice on the reals
statements.definition: Given (negative information about) a nonempty closed set $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, find a point of $A$. Equivalent to $\mathsf{C}_{2^{\mathbb{N}}} \times \mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}}$.
statements.instance: An enumeration of rational open intervals whose union is the complement of a nonempty closed $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$.
statements.solution: A point of $A$.

statements.label: \mathsf{UC}_{\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}}
statements.name: Unique closed choice on Baire space
statements.definition: Given a closed subset of $\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$ with exactly one element, find that element.
statements.instance: A tree $T \subseteq \mathbb{N}^{<\mathbb{N}}$ with exactly one infinite path.
statements.solution: The infinite path of $T$.

statements.label: \mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}}
statements.name: Closed choice on Baire space
statements.definition: Given a nonempty closed subset of $\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$, find an element. The single-valued problems below it are exactly the effectively Borel measurable functions; a candidate analogue of ATR in the Weihrauch lattice.
statements.instance: An ill-founded tree $T \subseteq \mathbb{N}^{<\mathbb{N}}$.
statements.solution: An infinite path through $T$.

statements.caution: “Unique choice” without qualification usually means unique choice on Baire space ([[ucnn]]) in the Weihrauch literature.
statements.label: \mathsf{UC}_{\mathbb{N}}
statements.name: Unique choice on the natural numbers
statements.definition: Given an enumeration of the complement of a singleton $\{n\} \subseteq \mathbb{N}$, find $n$.
statements.instance: An enumeration of $\mathbb{N} \setminus \{n\}$.
statements.solution: The number $n$.

statements.label: \mathsf{TC}_{\mathbb{N}}
statements.name: Total continuation of choice on the natural numbers
statements.definition: Given an enumeration of a set $B \subseteq \mathbb{N}$, find an element of $\mathbb{N} \setminus B$ if this set is nonempty, and any natural number otherwise.
statements.instance: An enumeration of a set $B \subseteq \mathbb{N}$.
statements.solution: An element of $\mathbb{N} \setminus B$ if there is one, any number otherwise.

statements.label: \mathsf{ACC}_{\mathbb{N}}
statements.name: All-or-co-unique choice on the natural numbers
statements.definition: Choice on $\mathbb{N}$ restricted to sets $A$ which are either $\mathbb{N}$ or $\mathbb{N} \setminus \{i\}$ for some $i$: given an enumeration of the complement of such an $A$, find an element of $A$.
statements.instance: An enumeration of the complement of a set $A \in \{\mathbb{N}\} \cup \{\mathbb{N} \setminus \{i\} : i \in \mathbb{N}\}$.
statements.solution: An element of $A$.

statements.label: \mathsf{NON}
statements.name: Non-computability problem
statements.definition: Given $p \in \mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$, find $q \in \mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$ which is not computable from $p$.
statements.instance: A sequence $p \in \mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$.
statements.solution: A sequence $q$ with $q \not\le_T p$.

statements.label: \mathsf{LLPO}'
statements.name: Jump of lesser limited principle of omniscience
statements.definition: The jump of $\mathsf{LLPO}$: an instance is a sequence converging to an instance of $\mathsf{LLPO}$ (in Baire space), with the same solutions.
statements.instance: A sequence converging (in Baire space) to an instance of $\mathsf{LLPO}$.
statements.solution: A solution of $\mathsf{LLPO}$ to the limit instance.

statements.label: \mathsf{DIS}
statements.name: Discontinuity problem
statements.definition: Given $p \in \mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$, find $q \in \mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$ different from $U(p)$, where $U$ is a fixed universal computable function.
statements.instance: A sequence $p \in \mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$.
statements.solution: A sequence $q \neq U(p)$.

statements.label: \mathsf{NRNG}
statements.name: Range non-equality problem
statements.definition: Given $p \in \mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$, find a set $A \in 2^\mathbb{N}$ with $A \neq \mathrm{range}(p - 1)$, the set of the numbers $n$ with $n + 1$ in the range of $p$.
statements.instance: A sequence $p \in \mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$.
statements.solution: A set $A \neq \mathrm{range}(p - 1)$.

statements.label: \mathsf{NMAJ}
statements.name: Non-majorization problem
statements.definition: Given $\langle i, p\rangle$, find $q \in \mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$ not majorized by $\varphi^p_i$: for some $n$, either $\varphi^p_i(n)$ is undefined or $\varphi^p_i(n) < q(n)$.
statements.instance: A pair $\langle i, p\rangle$ with $i \in \mathbb{N}$ and $p \in \mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$.
statements.solution: A function $q$ with $\varphi^p_i(n) \not\geq q(n)$ for some $n$.

statements.label: \mathsf{MEET}
statements.name: Meeting principle
statements.definition: Given $p \in \mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$, find $q \in \mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$ that meets every $p$-computable function: for every $r \leq_T p$ there is $n$ with $r(n) = q(n)$. Introduced by Hölzl, Raghavan, Stephan and Zhang in reverse mathematics.
statements.instance: A sequence $p \in \mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$.
statements.solution: A function $q$ with $(\forall r \leq_T p)(\exists n)\, r(n) = q(n)$.

statements.label: \mathsf{SORT}
statements.name: Binary sorting problem
statements.definition: Given $p \in 2^\mathbb{N}$, output $0^k1^\omega$ if $p$ contains exactly $k$ zeros, and $0^\omega$ if $p$ contains infinitely many zeros.
statements.instance: A sequence $p \in 2^\mathbb{N}$.
statements.solution: The sorted sequence ($0^k1^\omega$ or $0^\omega$).

statements.label: \mathsf{EC}
statements.name: Enumeration to characteristic function
statements.definition: Given an enumeration of a set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$, compute its characteristic function.
statements.instance: An enumeration $p$ of a set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ ($A = \mathrm{range}(p-1)$).
statements.solution: The characteristic function of $A$.

statements.label: \mathsf{PC}_{\mathbb{R}}
statements.name: Probabilistic choice on the reals
statements.definition: Given a closed set $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ of positive Lebesgue measure (by negative information), find a point of $A$.
statements.instance: A closed set $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ with $\mu(A) > 0$.
statements.solution: An element of $A$.

statements.label: \mathsf{TC}_{\mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}}
statements.name: Total continuation of choice on Baire space
statements.definition: Given a closed set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$ (by negative information), find a point of $A$ if $A$ is nonempty, and any point otherwise.
statements.instance: A closed set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$.
statements.solution: An element of $A$ if $A \neq \emptyset$, any point of $\mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$ otherwise.

statements.label: \mathsf{AUC}_{[0,1]}
statements.name: All-or-unique choice on [0,1]
statements.definition: Closed choice on $[0,1]$ restricted to the whole interval and singletons. Strongly Weihrauch equivalent to robust division $\mathsf{RDIV}$, $(x, y) \mapsto x / \max(x, y)$ if $y \neq 0$, any point of $[0,1]$ otherwise (Pauly).
statements.instance: A closed set $A \subseteq [0,1]$ (by negative information) which is $[0,1]$ or a singleton.
statements.solution: A point of $A$.

statements.label: \mathsf{PCC}_{[0,1]}
statements.name: Positive connected choice on [0,1]
statements.definition: Closed choice on $[0,1]$ restricted to connected sets of positive measure, that is, to proper closed intervals.
statements.instance: A proper closed interval $I \subseteq [0,1]$ (by negative information).
statements.solution: A point of $I$.

statements.label: \mathsf{NASH}
statements.name: Nash equilibria of bimatrix games
statements.definition: Given a finite bimatrix game with real payoffs, find a Nash equilibrium.
statements.instance: Two real $m \times n$ payoff matrices $A, B$.
statements.solution: A Nash equilibrium $(x, y)$ of the game $(A, B)$.

statements.label: \textsf{Lebesgue density lemma}
statements.name: Lebesgue density lemma
statements.definition: Given a closed $A \subseteq 2^\mathbb{N}$ of positive measure and $k$, find a word $w$ with $\mu(A \cap w2^\mathbb{N}) / 2^{-|w|} \geq 1 - 2^{-k}$.
statements.instance: A closed set $A \subseteq 2^\mathbb{N}$ of positive measure and a number $k$.
statements.solution: A word $w$ with $\mu(A \cap w2^\mathbb{N}) \geq (1 - 2^{-k}) 2^{-|w|}$.

statements.label: \tfrac{1}{2}\text{-}\mathsf{WWKL}
statements.name: Weak weak König's lemma with measure above 1/2
statements.definition: $\mathsf{WWKL}$ restricted to binary trees $T$ with $\mu([T]) > 1/2$ (an instance of $\varepsilon$-$\mathsf{WWKL}$; these problems get strictly weaker as $\varepsilon$ grows).
statements.instance: A binary tree $T$ with $\mu([T]) > 1/2$.
statements.solution: An infinite path through $T$.

statements.label: {*}\text{-}\mathsf{WWKL}
statements.name: Star weak weak König's lemma
statements.definition: Given $n$ and a binary tree $T$ with $\mu([T]) > 2^{-n}$, find an infinite path through $T$ (the uniform version of “$2^{-n}$-$\mathsf{WWKL}$ for every $n$”).
statements.instance: A number $n$ and a binary tree $T$ with $\mu([T]) > 2^{-n}$.
statements.solution: An infinite path through $T$.

statements.label: (1-{*})\text{-}\mathsf{WWKL}
statements.name: Lower star weak weak König's lemma
statements.definition: Given a sequence of binary trees $(T_n)_n$ with $\mu([T_n]) > 1 - 2^{-n}$ for every $n$, find some $n$ and an infinite path through $T_n$.
statements.instance: A sequence $(T_n)_n$ of binary trees with $\mu([T_n]) > 1 - 2^{-n}$.
statements.solution: A pair $(n, p)$ with $p \in [T_n]$.

statements.label: \chi_{\Pi^1_1}
statements.name: Characteristic function of a Π¹₁-complete set
statements.definition: Given a tree $T \subseteq \mathbb{N}^{<\mathbb{N}}$, decide whether $T$ is well-founded. A single-valued function which is not effectively Borel measurable, hence not Weihrauch reducible to $\mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}}$.
statements.instance: A tree $T \subseteq \mathbb{N}^{<\mathbb{N}}$.
statements.solution: 1 if $T$ is well-founded, 0 otherwise.

statements.label: \mathsf{NHA}
statements.name: Non-hyperarithmeticity problem
statements.definition: Given $p \in \mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$, find some $q$ that is not hyperarithmetical relative to $p$.
statements.instance: A point $p \in \mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$.
statements.solution: A point $q$ not hyperarithmetical in $p$.

statements.label: \mathsf{sTC}_{\mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}}
statements.name: Strong total continuation of choice on Baire space
statements.definition: Given a tree $T \subseteq \mathbb{N}^{<\mathbb{N}}$, output a bit $b$ telling whether $T$ is ill-founded and, if it is, an infinite path through $T$.
statements.instance: A tree $T \subseteq \mathbb{N}^{<\mathbb{N}}$.
statements.solution: $(0, x)$ for any $x$ if $[T] = \emptyset$; $(1, x)$ with $x \in [T]$ otherwise.

statements.label: \Sigma^0_1\text{-}\mathsf{RT}
statements.name: Open Ramsey theorem
statements.definition: Given an open set $P \subseteq [\mathbb{N}]^{\mathbb{N}}$, find a homogeneous solution: an infinite set $H$ whose infinite subsets are all in $P$ or all outside $P$. The problem form of the open Ramsey theorem (equivalent to $\mathsf{ATR}_0$).
statements.instance: An open set $P \subseteq [\mathbb{N}]^{\mathbb{N}}$.
statements.solution: An infinite $H$ with $[H]^{\mathbb{N}} \subseteq P$ or $[H]^{\mathbb{N}} \cap P = \emptyset$.

statements.label: \mathsf{FindHS}_{\Sigma^0_1}
statements.name: Strong open Ramsey theorem (open side)
statements.definition: Given an open set $P \subseteq [\mathbb{N}]^{\mathbb{N}}$ with a homogeneous solution landing in $P$, find such a solution.
statements.instance: An open set $P$ having some $H$ with $[H]^{\mathbb{N}} \subseteq P$.
statements.solution: An infinite $H$ with $[H]^{\mathbb{N}} \subseteq P$.

statements.label: \mathsf{FindHS}_{\Pi^0_1}
statements.name: Strong open Ramsey theorem (closed side)
statements.definition: Given an open set $P \subseteq [\mathbb{N}]^{\mathbb{N}}$ with a homogeneous solution avoiding $P$, find such a solution.
statements.instance: An open set $P$ having some $H$ with $[H]^{\mathbb{N}} \cap P = \emptyset$.
statements.solution: An infinite $H$ with $[H]^{\mathbb{N}} \cap P = \emptyset$.

statements.label: \mathsf{wFindHS}_{\Sigma^0_1}
statements.name: Weak open Ramsey theorem (open side)
