statements.definition: $\mathsf{FindHS}_{\Sigma^0_1}$ restricted to open sets $P$ all of whose homogeneous solutions land in $P$.
statements.instance: An open set $P$ such that every homogeneous solution $H$ has $[H]^{\mathbb{N}} \subseteq P$.
statements.solution: A homogeneous solution of $P$.

statements.label: \mathsf{wFindHS}_{\Pi^0_1}
statements.name: Weak open Ramsey theorem (closed side)
statements.definition: $\mathsf{FindHS}_{\Pi^0_1}$ restricted to open sets $P$ with no homogeneous solution landing in $P$. It lies strictly above $\mathsf{UC}_{\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}}$, below $\mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}}$, and not below $\mathsf{ATR}_2$.
statements.instance: An open set $P$ such that every homogeneous solution $H$ has $[H]^{\mathbb{N}} \cap P = \emptyset$.
statements.solution: A homogeneous solution of $P$.

statements.label: \Delta^0_1\text{-}\mathsf{RT}
statements.name: Clopen Ramsey theorem
statements.definition: Given a clopen set $D \subseteq [\mathbb{N}]^{\mathbb{N}}$ (by names of it and its complement), find a homogeneous solution.
statements.instance: A clopen set $D \subseteq [\mathbb{N}]^{\mathbb{N}}$.
statements.solution: An infinite $H$ with $[H]^{\mathbb{N}} \subseteq D$ or $[H]^{\mathbb{N}} \cap D = \emptyset$.

statements.label: \mathsf{FindHS}_{\Delta^0_1}
statements.name: Strong clopen Ramsey theorem
statements.definition: Given a clopen set $D$ with a homogeneous solution landing in $D$, find such a solution.
statements.instance: A clopen set $D$ having some $H$ with $[H]^{\mathbb{N}} \subseteq D$.
statements.solution: An infinite $H$ with $[H]^{\mathbb{N}} \subseteq D$.

statements.label: \mathsf{wFindHS}_{\Delta^0_1}
statements.name: Weak clopen Ramsey theorem
statements.definition: $\mathsf{FindHS}_{\Delta^0_1}$ restricted to clopen sets $D$ all of whose homogeneous solutions land in $D$.
statements.instance: A clopen set $D$ such that every homogeneous solution $H$ has $[H]^{\mathbb{N}} \subseteq D$.
statements.solution: A homogeneous solution of $D$.

statements.label: \Sigma^1_1\text{-}\mathsf{WKL}
statements.name: Σ¹₁ weak König's lemma
statements.definition: Given a $\Sigma^1_1$ code of an infinite binary tree $T \subseteq 2^{<\omega}$, find an infinite path through $T$. Weihrauch equivalent to $\Pi^1_1$ separation, to $\Pi^1_1\text{-}\mathsf{DNC}_2$ and to the parallelization of $\Sigma^1_1$ choice on $\{0,1\}$; strictly between $\mathsf{UC}_{\mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}}$ and $\mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}}$.
statements.instance: A $\Sigma^1_1$ code of an infinite binary tree $T$.
statements.solution: An infinite path through $T$.

statements.caution: As Weihrauch problems, Σ¹₁-Sep (≡ UC_ℕℕ, Theorem 3.11 of [@kiharamarconepauly2020]) lies strictly below Π¹₁-Sep, while as sentences Σ¹₁ separation ([[sigma11-sep]]) is equivalent to ATR₀ and Π¹₁ separation is strictly weaker than ATR₀.
statements.label: \Pi^1_1\text{-}\mathsf{Sep}
statements.name: Π¹₁ separation (Weihrauch problem)
statements.definition: Given $\Pi^1_1$ codes of disjoint sets $A, B \subseteq \mathbb{N}$, find a set $C$ with $A \subseteq C$ and $B \cap C = \emptyset$.
statements.instance: Two disjoint $\Pi^1_1$ sets $A, B \subseteq \mathbb{N}$, given by codes.
statements.solution: A set separating $A$ from $B$.

statements.label: \Sigma^1_1\text{-}\mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}}
statements.name: Σ¹₁ choice on the natural numbers
statements.definition: Given a $\Sigma^1_1$ code of a nonempty set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$, find an element of $A$. Weihrauch equivalent to the first-order part of $\mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}}$.
statements.instance: A $\Sigma^1_1$ code of a nonempty $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$.
statements.solution: An element of $A$.

statements.label: \Sigma^1_1\text{-}\mathsf{WWKL}
statements.name: Σ¹₁ weak weak König's lemma
statements.definition: Given a $\Sigma^1_1$ code of a binary tree $T$ with $\mu([T]) > 0$, find an infinite path through $T$.
statements.instance: A $\Sigma^1_1$ code of a binary tree $T$ with $\mu([T]) > 0$.
statements.solution: An infinite path through $T$.

statements.caution: PTT₁ is a perfect tree theorem; PTT with a superscript, as in PTT², is the polarized tree theorem ([[ptt2]]).
statements.label: \mathsf{PTT}_1
statements.name: One-sided perfect tree theorem
statements.definition: Given a tree $T \subseteq \mathbb{N}^{<\mathbb{N}}$ with uncountably many paths, find a perfect subtree of $T$.
statements.instance: A tree $T \subseteq \mathbb{N}^{<\mathbb{N}}$ with $[T]$ uncountable.
statements.solution: A perfect subtree of $T$.

statements.label: \mathsf{List}
statements.name: Listing countable closed subsets of Baire space
statements.definition: Given a countable closed set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$, enumerate its elements, together with its cardinality (the weak version $\mathsf{wList}$, without the cardinality, is equivalent).
statements.instance: A countable closed set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$.
statements.solution: A pair $n\langle p_0, p_1, \dots \rangle$: if $n = 0$ the $p_i$ are distinct and $A = \{p_i : i \in \mathbb{N}\}$, otherwise $|A| = n - 1$ and $A = \{p_i : i < n - 1\}$.

statements.label: \mathsf{FindWS}_\Sigma
statements.name: Winning strategies for the open player
statements.definition: Given an open game on $\mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$ in which Player 2 has no winning strategy, find a winning strategy for Player 1 (the open player).
statements.instance: An open set $W \subseteq \mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$ (the winning condition of Player 1) such that Player 2 has no winning strategy.
statements.solution: A winning strategy for Player 1.

statements.label: \mathsf{FindWS}_\Pi
statements.name: Winning strategies for the closed player
statements.definition: Given an open game on $\mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$ in which Player 1 has no winning strategy, find a winning strategy for Player 2 (the closed player).
statements.instance: An open set $W \subseteq \mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$ such that Player 1 has no winning strategy.
statements.solution: A winning strategy for Player 2.

statements.label: \mathsf{Det}_\Sigma
statements.name: Open determinacy (Nash equilibria of open games)
statements.definition: Given an open game on $\mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$, find a pair of strategies $(\sigma, \tau)$ such that either $\sigma$ is winning for Player 1 or $\tau$ is winning for Player 2, without being told which player wins.
statements.instance: An open set $W \subseteq \mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$, the winning condition of Player 1.
statements.solution: A pair of strategies $(\sigma, \tau)$, one of which is winning.

statements.caution: PTT₂ is a perfect tree theorem; PTT²₂ (superscript 2) is the polarized tree theorem for pairs and two colors ([[ptt22]]).
statements.label: \mathsf{PTT}_2
statements.name: Two-sided perfect tree theorem
statements.definition: Given a tree $T \subseteq \mathbb{N}^{<\mathbb{N}}$, find either a perfect subtree of $T$ or a listing of $[T]$ together with its cardinality.
statements.instance: A tree $T \subseteq \mathbb{N}^{<\mathbb{N}}$.
statements.solution: A pair $(T', n\langle p_0, p_1, \dots \rangle)$ such that $T'$ is a perfect subtree of $T$, or the second component lists $[T]$ as in $\mathsf{List}$.

statements.label: \mathsf{wPTT}_2
statements.name: Weak two-sided perfect tree theorem
statements.definition: Like $\mathsf{PTT}_2$, with a listing of $[T]$ that carries no information on its cardinality.
statements.instance: A tree $T \subseteq \mathbb{N}^{<\mathbb{N}}$.
statements.solution: A pair $(T', \langle b_0 p_0, b_1 p_1, \dots \rangle)$ such that $T'$ is a perfect subtree of $T$ or $[T] = \{p_i : b_i \neq 0\}$.

statements.caution: For Weihrauch reducibility it matters whether the number of colors is part of the instance. Here RT¹_ℕ receives only the coloring, as in Goh, Pauly and Valenti [@gohpaulyvalenti2021], while RT¹_{<∞} ([[rt1inf]]) also receives the bound k. Check which convention a paper uses.
statements.label: \mathsf{RT}^1_{\mathbb{N}}
statements.name: Pigeonhole principle without a bound on the colors
statements.definition: Given a coloring $c : \mathbb{N} \to k$ for some $k$ which is not given, find an infinite homogeneous set.
statements.instance: A coloring $c : \mathbb{N} \to k$ for some $k$ (without $k$).
statements.solution: An infinite set on which $c$ is constant.

statements.label: \Pi^1_1\text{-}\mathsf{Bound}
statements.name: Bound for finite Π¹₁ sets
statements.definition: Given a finite $\Pi^1_1$ subset of $\mathbb{N}$, find an upper bound for it. Strongly Weihrauch equivalent to $\Sigma^1_1$ choice on $\mathbb{N}$ for cofinite sets, and Weihrauch equivalent to the first-order part of $\mathsf{DS}$.
statements.instance: A finite $\Pi^1_1$ set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$.
statements.solution: A number $n$ with $m \notin A$ for every $m \geq n$.

statements.label: \Sigma^1_1\text{-}\mathsf{DS}
statements.name: Descending sequences in Σ¹₁ linear orders
statements.definition: $\mathsf{DS}$ for ill-founded linear orders given by a $\Sigma^1_1$ code.
statements.instance: An ill-founded linear order given by a $\Sigma^1_1$ code.
statements.solution: An infinite descending sequence.

statements.label: \Sigma^1_1\text{-}\mathsf{BS}
statements.name: Bad sequences in Σ¹₁ quasi-orders
statements.definition: $\mathsf{BS}$ for non-well quasi-orders given by a $\Sigma^1_1$ code.
statements.instance: A quasi-order which is not a well quasi-order, given by a $\Sigma^1_1$ code.
statements.solution: An infinite bad sequence.

statements.label: \mathsf{ATR}_2
statements.name: Two-sided arithmetical transfinite recursion
statements.definition: Given a linear order $L$ and a set $A$, produce either an infinite $<_L$-descending sequence or a jump hierarchy on $L$ starting with $A$, indicating which. Strictly between $\mathsf{UC}_{\mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}}$ and $\mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}}$.
statements.instance: A linear order $L$ and a set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$.
statements.solution: An infinite descending sequence in $L$, or a jump hierarchy $\langle X_a \rangle_{a \in L}$ with $X_0 = A$.

statements.label: \mathsf{CWO}_2
statements.name: Two-sided comparability of well-orderings
statements.definition: Given linear orders $L$ and $M$, produce an embedding of one onto an initial segment of the other, or an infinite descending sequence in one of them, indicating which.
statements.instance: Two linear orders $L$ and $M$.
statements.solution: An embedding of one onto an initial segment of the other, or a descending sequence in one of them.

statements.label: \mathsf{WCWO}_2
statements.name: Two-sided weak comparability of well-orderings
statements.definition: Given linear orders $L$ and $M$, produce an embedding of one into the other, or an infinite descending sequence in one of them, indicating which.
statements.instance: Two linear orders $L$ and $M$.
statements.solution: An embedding of one into the other, or a descending sequence in one of them.

statements.label: \mathsf{KDT}
statements.name: König's duality theorem (Weihrauch problem)
statements.definition: Given a countable bipartite graph, produce a König cover $(C, M)$: a vertex cover $C$ and a matching $M$ such that $C$ consists of exactly one vertex from each edge of $M$. The problem form of the Podewski–Steffens theorem.
statements.instance: A countable bipartite graph $G$.
statements.solution: A König cover of $G$.

statements.label: \mathsf{LBT}
statements.name: Low basis theorem (Weihrauch problem)
statements.definition: Given an infinite binary tree $T$, find a path $p \in [T]$ with $p' \leq_T T'$. Strictly above $\mathsf{WKL}$ and Weihrauch incomparable with $\mathsf{C}_\mathbb{R}$.
statements.instance: An infinite binary tree $T$.
statements.solution: A path $p \in [T]$ with $p' \leq_T T'$.

statements.label: 1\text{-}\mathsf{WGEN}
statements.name: Weak 1-genericity problem
statements.definition: Given $q \in 2^\mathbb{N}$, find some $p$ weakly 1-generic relative to $q$.
statements.instance: A point $q \in 2^\mathbb{N}$.
statements.solution: A point $p$ weakly 1-generic in $q$.

statements.label: \mathsf{KPT}
statements.name: Kleene–Post theorem (Weihrauch problem)
statements.definition: Given $r$, find a pair $\langle p, q \rangle \geq_T r$ with $p$ and $q$ Turing incomparable.
statements.instance: A point $r \in \mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$.
statements.solution: A pair $\langle p, q \rangle$ with $r \leq_T \langle p, q \rangle$ and $p \mid_T q$.

statements.label: \mathsf{DNC}_3
statements.name: Diagonally non-computable functions with 3 values
statements.definition: Given $p$, find $q \in 3^\mathbb{N}$ with $q(n) \neq \varphi^p_n(n)$ for every $n$. Strongly Weihrauch equivalent to the parallelization of $\mathsf{ACC}_3$; strictly between $\mathsf{DNC}_\mathbb{N}$ and $\mathsf{DNC}_2 \equiv_{\mathrm{sW}} \mathsf{WKL}$.
statements.instance: A point $p \in \mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$.
statements.solution: A function $q \in 3^\mathbb{N}$ with $q(n) \neq \varphi^p_n(n)$ for all $n$.

statements.label: \mathsf{COH}^+
statements.name: Cohesiveness for enumerated sequences
statements.definition: $\mathsf{COH}$ with the sets $R_i$ given by enumerations (positive information) instead of characteristic functions.
statements.instance: A sequence of enumerations of sets $R_0, R_1, \dots \subseteq \mathbb{N}$.
statements.solution: A set cohesive for $(R_i)_i$.

statements.label: \mathsf{WBWT}_\mathbb{R}
statements.name: Weak Bolzano–Weierstrass theorem
statements.definition: Given a bounded sequence of reals, find a sequence converging to a Cauchy name of one of its cluster points ($\mathsf{BWT}_\mathbb{R}$ with the jump of the Cauchy representation on the output).
statements.instance: A bounded sequence $(x_n)_n$ of reals.
statements.solution: A sequence converging to a name of a cluster point of $(x_n)_n$.

statements.label: \mathsf{SBWT}_\mathbb{R}
statements.name: Subsequential Bolzano–Weierstrass theorem
statements.definition: Given a bounded sequence $(x_i)_i$ of reals, find a strictly increasing $s$ such that $(x_{s(n)})_n$ converges.
statements.instance: A bounded sequence $(x_i)_i$ of reals.
statements.solution: A strictly increasing $s \in \mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$ with $(x_{s(n)})_n$ convergent.

statements.label: \mathsf{DNC}^*
statements.name: Finitary DNC problem
statements.definition: Given, for every $k \geq 2$, an instance of $\widehat{\mathsf{ACC}_k}$ (that is, of $\mathsf{DNC}_k$), find some $k$ and a solution of the $k$-th instance. Strictly above both $\mathsf{PA}$ and $\mathsf{DNC}_\mathbb{N}$.
statements.instance: Sequences $(A_{n,k})_{n}$ for $k \geq 2$, with $A_{n,k} \subseteq k$ and $|k \setminus A_{n,k}| \leq 1$, given by negative information.
statements.solution: A pair $\langle k, p \rangle$ with $p(n) \in A_{n,k}$ for every $n$.

statements.label: \mathsf{IPAC}^+
statements.name: Improper PAC learning from positive information
statements.definition: Given a nonempty closed concept class $C \subseteq 2^\mathbb{N}$ by positive information and a bound $d$ on its VC dimension, find a learner (with arbitrary hypotheses) and a sample complexity with which it PAC learns $C$. Strongly Weihrauch equivalent to finding a witness function for $C$.
statements.instance: A closed class $C \subseteq 2^\mathbb{N}$, $C \neq \emptyset$, given by positive information, and $d \geq \mathrm{VCdim}(C)$.
statements.solution: A learner $A$ and a sample complexity $m$ with which $A$ improperly PAC learns $C$.

statements.label: \mathsf{RPAC}
statements.name: Relative PAC learning
statements.definition: Given closed classes $C \subseteq H \subseteq 2^\mathbb{N}$ ($C$ by positive, $H$ by negative information) and $d \geq \mathrm{VCdim}(C)$, find a learner into $H$ and a sample complexity with which it PAC learns $C$ relative to $H$.
statements.instance: Closed classes $\emptyset \neq C \subseteq H \subseteq 2^\mathbb{N}$ and $d \geq \mathrm{VCdim}(C)$.
statements.solution: A learner $A : S \to H$ and a sample complexity $m$ with which $A$ PAC learns $C$ relative to $H$.

statements.label: \mathsf{ATR}
statements.name: Arithmetical transfinite recursion (problem)
statements.caution: The Weihrauch problem of Kihara, Marcone and Pauly [@kiharamarconepauly2020]; the sentence ATR₀ of reverse mathematics is [[atr]].
statements.definition: Given a set $Z$, a well-order $X$ and an arithmetical operator (an index of an arithmetical formula), return the hierarchy obtained by iterating the operator along $X$ starting from $Z$. A single-valued problem, strongly Weihrauch equivalent to $\mathsf{UC}_{\mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}}$.
statements.instance: A set $Z$, a well-order $X$ and an index of an arithmetical formula.
statements.solution: The unique hierarchy along $X$ starting from $Z$.

statements.label: \mathsf{BCT}_0
statements.name: Baire category theorem (negative information, point)
statements.definition: Given a sequence of nowhere dense closed sets by negative information, find a point outside their union.
statements.instance: A sequence of nowhere dense closed sets, given by negative information.
statements.solution: A point outside their union.

statements.label: \mathsf{BCT}_1
statements.name: Baire category theorem (negative information, index)
statements.definition: Given a sequence of closed sets by negative information whose union is the whole space, find an index of a set with nonempty interior.
statements.instance: A sequence of closed sets covering the space, given by negative information.
statements.solution: An $i$ such that the $i$-th set has nonempty interior.

statements.instance: A sequence of closed sets covering the space, given by positive information.
statements.solution: An $i$ such that the $i$-th set has nonempty interior.

Over RCA₀*, arithmetical comprehension turns a Σ⁰₁ formula into a set, and the Δ⁰₀ induction axiom applied to that set yields Σ⁰₁ induction; hence ACA proves IΣ⁰₁, i.e. RCA₀.
Given f : [ℕ]² → 3, merge colors 1 and 2 into one. A set homogeneous for the merged 2-coloring avoids either color 0 or colors 1 and 2 for f, so it is thin for f.
Given f : [ℕ]² → 4, merge colors 2 and 3. A set avoiding one color of the merged 3-coloring avoids color 0, color 1, or both colors 2 and 3 for f.
Given f : [ℕ]² → ℕ, let g = min(f, 3). A set on which g avoids a color c < 3 is one on which f avoids c; if g avoids 3, then f takes only the values 0, 1, 2.
Given f : [ℕ]³ → 2, color a quadruple by the color of its first three elements; a homogeneous set for this coloring of quadruples is homogeneous for f.

By Corollary 3.4, every X-computable instance of UC_NN has only solutions hyperarithmetical in X, so X ⊕ solution is hyperarithmetical. The ω-model HYP satisfies UC_NN, since solutions of X-computable instances are hyperarithmetical in X by Corollary 3.4. It fails C_NN by Kleene's computable nonempty Π⁰₁ class without hyperarithmetical members. (From Section 3, after Theorem 3.5, with Corollary 3.4 of [@kiharamarconepauly2020].)

Given f : ℕ → 3, color x by 0 if f(x) < 2 and by 1 otherwise. A homogeneous set of color 0 avoids color 2 of f, one of color 1 avoids colors 0 and 1.

STS²₄ is TS²₄ restricted to stable colorings (Definition 8.0.2 of [@patey2016c]).
Merge colors 2 and 3 of a stable f : [ℕ]² → 4; the resulting 3-coloring is stable and a set thin for it is thin for f.
Given a stable f : [ℕ]² → ℕ, the coloring min(f, 3) : [ℕ]² → 4 is stable, and a set avoiding one of its colors avoids a color of f.
RSAT_2-branching is RSAT restricted to 2-branching sets of clauses (Definition 11.2.4 of [@patey2016c]).

Property P1 gives a computable instance that is solved by only a small class of oracles. A computable solution would be computed by every oracle, and that class is 2^ω, which is not small. So some computable instance has no computable solution. (From Theorem 4.20 of [@astoretal2026].)

Proposition 5.5 shows BCT2 is strongly parallelizable. Corollary 8.3 gives Π01G ≡sW BCT2 on Cantor space, and this property is invariant under ≡sW. (From Proposition 5.5 and Corollary 8.3 of [@brattkahendtlasskreuzer2018].)

Proposition 5.5 shows BCT2 is strongly idempotent, hence idempotent. Corollary 8.3 gives Π01G ≡sW BCT2, and idempotency is preserved under equivalence. (From Proposition 5.5 and Corollary 8.3 of [@brattkahendtlasskreuzer2018].)

The paper states that BCT2 and its jumps are not cylinders. Corollary 8.3 gives Π01G ≡sW BCT2, so Π01G is not a cylinder either. (From Section 5 after Lemma 5.4, and Corollary 8.3 of [@brattkahendtlasskreuzer2018].)
The paper states ACC_n ≰W PA for n ≥ 2, by Corollary 4.7. Take n = 2 with LLPO ≡sW ACC_2. (From Section 5, after Fact 5.7 of [@brattka2021].)

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{RT}^2_2$ imply $\mathsf{WKL}_0$ over $\mathsf{RCA}_0$? Does $\mathsf{RT}^2_{<\infty}$?
questions.context: Seetapun [@seetapunslaman1995] showed that RT²₂ admits cone avoidance, so RT²₂ does not imply ACA₀. Whether it implies the much weaker WKL₀ — equivalently, whether every instance can be solved without computing a PA degree — remained open until Liu [@liu2012] proved PA avoidance for RT²₂. Since ω-models of RT²₂ are models of RT²_{<∞}, the second part follows.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{SRT}^2_2$ imply $\mathsf{RT}^2_2$ (equivalently, $\mathsf{COH}$)? Does $\mathsf{SRT}^2_{<\infty}$ imply $\mathsf{RT}^2_{<\infty}$ (equivalently, $\mathsf{COH}$)?
questions.context: Cholak, Jockusch and Slaman [@cholakjockuschslaman2001] decomposed RT²₂ into its stable part SRT²₂ and its cohesive part COH, and asked whether the stable part alone suffices. This became one of the central questions of the field. Chong, Slaman and Yang [@chongslamanyang2014] gave a negative answer using a non-standard model in which every set is low; the question for ω-models — that is, for computability theory proper — was answered negatively by Monin and Patey [@moninpatey2021].

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{RT}^2_2$ imply $\mathsf{I}\Sigma^0_2$? Does $\mathsf{RT}^2_{<\infty}$ imply $\mathsf{I}\Sigma^0_3$?
questions.context: RT²₂ implies BΣ⁰₂ [@hirst1987] and is Π¹₁-conservative over RCA₀ + IΣ⁰₂ [@cholakjockuschslaman2001], so its first-order part lies between BΣ⁰₂ and IΣ⁰₂. Chong, Slaman and Yang [@chongslamanyang2017] showed that it does not reach IΣ⁰₂; Slaman and Yokoyama [@slamanyokoyama2018] answered the question for arbitrarily many colors.

questions.question: Is $\mathsf{RCA}_0 + \mathsf{RT}^2_2$ $\Pi^0_2$-conservative over $\mathsf{RCA}_0$? In particular, does it prove the totality of the Ackermann function, or the consistency of $\mathsf{I}\Sigma_1$? Does it prove that $\omega^\omega$ is well-ordered?
questions.answer: Yes. RT²₂ (even with WKL₀) is ∀Π⁰₃-conservative over RCA₀, so it proves no new Π⁰₂ sentence; nor does it prove that ω^ω is well-ordered.
questions.context: This asks whether RT²₂ is "finitistically reducible": whether the Π⁰₂ consequences of RT²₂, which correspond to provably total functions, are already those of IΣ⁰₁ (primitive recursive functions). Patey and Yokoyama [@pateyyokoyama2018] answered positively by a model-theoretic argument based on a new notion of largeness of finite sets.

questions.question: Does every $\Delta^0_2$ set have an infinite low subset in it or in its complement? Equivalently, does every computable stable coloring of pairs have an infinite low homogeneous set?
questions.answer: No — there is a Δ⁰₂ set with no infinite low subset in either it or its complement.
questions.context: A relativizable positive answer would have separated SRT²₂ from RT²₂, since RT²₂ has computable instances without low₂ solutions [@jockusch1972]. The answer is negative [@downeyetal2001], which is why the separation of SRT²₂ from RT²₂ needed other ideas: Chong, Slaman and Yang [@chongslamanyang2014] built a non-standard model in which every set is low.

questions.question: For every 2-coloring $C$ of $[\mathbb{N}]^2$ which is not of PA degree, is there an infinite homogeneous set $H$ such that $C \oplus H$ is not of PA degree?
questions.context: A relativizable positive answer gives an ω-model of RT²₂ with no PA degree, hence separates RT²₂ from WKL₀ (see the question on RT²₂ and WKL₀). Liu [@liu2012] proved it with a new forcing notion whose conditions are Mathias conditions with a Π⁰₁ class of reservoirs.

questions.question: Does the chain/antichain principle $\mathsf{CAC}$ imply $\mathsf{RT}^2_2$?
questions.context: CAC follows easily from RT²₂ by coloring pairs according to comparability. Hirschfeldt and Shore [@hirschfeldtshore2007] showed that CAC is much weaker: it has an ω-model with no DNR function, while RT²₂ implies DNR.

questions.question: Does the free set theorem $\mathsf{FS}^2$, or the thin set theorem $\mathsf{TS}^2$, imply $\mathsf{RT}^2_2$? Does $\mathsf{FS}^2 + \mathsf{WKL}_0$? Does $\mathsf{FS}^2$ imply $\mathsf{B}\Sigma^0_2$?
questions.context: The free set and thin set theorems [@cholaketal2005] are consequences of Ramsey's theorem in which the homogeneity requirement is weakened. They are natural candidates for principles strictly between RCA₀ and RT²₂.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{FS}^2 + \mathsf{CAC}$ imply $\mathsf{RT}^2_2$? Does $\mathsf{FS}^2 + \mathsf{COH}$?
questions.context: Combining a free set principle with a principle handling the "unstable" part of colorings is a natural attempt to recover RT²₂, by analogy with RT²₂ ⇔ SRT²₂ + COH [@cholakjockuschslaman2001].

questions.question: Do the free set or thin set theorems for exponent $k \ge 3$, or for all exponents, imply $\mathsf{ACA}_0$?
questions.context: Ramsey's theorem for triples implies ACA₀ [@jockusch1972], unlike RT²₂. Whether the weaker free set and thin set theorems behave like Ramsey's theorem for pairs at every exponent was settled by Wang [@wang2014b], who showed that they admit strong cone avoidance at every exponent.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{SADS}$ imply $\mathsf{SCAC}$?
questions.context: Hirschfeldt and Shore [@hirschfeldtshore2007] introduced the stable versions of ADS and CAC and showed that SCAC implies SADS.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{CRT}^2_2$, or even $\mathsf{CADS}$, imply $\mathsf{COH}$?
questions.context: COH implies both CADS and the cohesive Ramsey theorem CRT²₂ [@hirschfeldtshore2007]. Over ω-models, and even for Weihrauch reducibility, CADS is equivalent to COH [@fioricaronesshafersolda2022], and CADS implies COH over RCA₀ + BΣ⁰₂ [@dzhafarovmummert2022]; so a negative answer over RCA₀ would have to use non-standard models.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{CADS}$ imply $\mathsf{CRT}^2_2$?
questions.context: A companion of the question whether CADS implies COH: CRT²₂ lies between COH and CADS [@hirschfeldtshore2007].

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{SADS}$, or even $\mathsf{PART}$, imply $\mathsf{B}\Sigma^0_2$?
questions.context: SCAC implies BΣ⁰₂ [@hirschfeldtshore2007], and the question asks how far down this goes. Chong, Lempp and Yang [@chonglemppyang2010] showed that PART, and hence SADS, implies BΣ⁰₂.

questions.question: Are the principles weaker than $\mathsf{ACA}_0$ studied by Hirschfeldt and Shore (other than those following from $\mathsf{WKL}_0$ or $\mathsf{COH}$) $\Pi^1_1$-conservative, or at least arithmetically conservative, over $\mathsf{B}\Sigma^0_2$?
questions.answer: COH, ADS, CAC and their stable versions are Π¹₁-conservative over RCA₀ + BΣ⁰₂.
questions.context: Proving conservation over BΣ⁰₂ is harder than over IΣ⁰₂, since the usual forcing arguments use Σ⁰₂-induction. Chong, Slaman and Yang [@chongslamanyang2012] developed techniques for models of BΣ⁰₂ and showed conservation for the main principles weaker than RT²₂.

questions.question: Is there an exponent $n$ such that the rainbow Ramsey theorem $\mathsf{RRT}^n_2$ implies $\mathsf{ACA}_0$?
questions.context: Ramsey's theorem RTⁿ₂ implies ACA₀ for every n ≥ 3, but the rainbow Ramsey theorem is much weaker: Csima and Mileti [@csimamileti2009] showed RRT²₂ follows from 2-randomness. Wang [@wang2013] showed that RRT³₂ does not imply ACA₀, and later that no exponent does [@wang2014b].

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{IPT}^2_2$ (or $\mathsf{IPT}^2_2 + \mathsf{B}\Sigma^0_2$) imply $\mathsf{RT}^2_2$? Does $\mathsf{IPT}^2_2$ imply $\mathsf{B}\Sigma^0_2$? Is $\mathsf{IPT}^2_2$ implied by $\mathsf{SRT}^2_2$ over ω-models? For arbitrarily many colors, does $\mathsf{SRT}^2_{<\infty}$ imply $\mathsf{IPT}^2_{<\infty}$, and does $\mathsf{IPT}^2_{<\infty}$ imply $\mathsf{RT}^2_{<\infty}$?
questions.context: The increasing polarized Ramsey theorem IPT²₂ [@dzhafarovhirst2009] lies between SRT²₂ and RT²₂. An equivalence between IPT²₂ + BΣ⁰₂ and RT²₂ would follow from SRT²₂ ⇒ RT²₂, so separating them is at least as hard as the SRT²₂ vs. RT²₂ question.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{SIPT}^2_2$ or $\mathsf{SPT}^2_2$ imply $\mathsf{SRT}^2_2$ (equivalently, $\mathsf{B}\Sigma^0_2$)?
questions.context: Dzhafarov and Hirst [@dzhafarovhirst2009] showed that the stable polarized principles together with BΣ⁰₂ imply SRT²₂. Chong, Lempp and Yang [@chonglemppyang2010] showed that they imply BΣ⁰₂ themselves.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{COH}$ (or $\mathsf{CADS}$) imply the atomic model theorem $\mathsf{AMT}$? Does $\mathsf{CADS}$ imply $\mathsf{OPT}$?
questions.context: Hirschfeldt, Shore and Slaman [@hirschfeldtshoreslaman2009] placed AMT below SADS and OPT (omitting partial types) below AMT. COH and CADS are the natural "unstable" principles to compare with them.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{AMT}$ imply $\overline{\mathsf{D}}_2\mathsf{IP}$? Does $\mathsf{OPT}$? Does $\overline{\mathsf{D}}_2\mathsf{IP}$ imply $\mathsf{FIP}$?
questions.context: Dzhafarov and Mummert [@dzhafarovmummert2013] studied intersection principles for families of sets. The principles D_nIP asking for a maximal subfamily with the D_n intersection property are equivalent to ACA₀; their weak versions D̄_nIP (written D_nIP in [@dzhafarovmummert2010] and nIP in [@cholakdowneyigusa2017]) form a hierarchy below the finite intersection principle FIP, close to the atomic model theorem. AMT implies D̄₂IP over RCA₀ + IΣ⁰₂.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{ASRAM}$ imply $\mathsf{SRAM}$? Does $\mathsf{SRT}^2_2$ imply $\mathsf{ASRAM}$, or conversely? Does $\mathsf{ASRT}^2_2$ imply $\mathsf{WWKL}_0$?
questions.context: Dzhafarov [@dzhafarov2011] introduced the "almost" versions of stable Ramsey principles, inspired by the reverse mathematics of the sorites paradox.

questions.question: Unique choice on Baire space is Weihrauch-equivalent to closed choice on Baire space, $\mathsf{UC}_{\mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}} \equiv_W \mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}}$.
questions.context: C_ℕ^ℕ and UC_ℕ^ℕ are the Weihrauch counterparts of ATR₀-like principles [@brattkadebrechtpauly2012]. The conjecture was refuted: unique choice is strictly weaker than closed choice on Baire space.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{DNR}$ imply the Ramsey-type weak König's lemma $\mathsf{RWKL}$?
questions.context: Flood [@flood2012] introduced RWKL, which asks for an infinite set homogeneous for a path of a binary tree, and showed that it is implied by SRT²₂ and implies DNR.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{D}^2_2$ imply $\mathsf{P}^2_2$?
questions.context: A question from Flood's study of Ramsey-type versions of König's lemma [@flood2012].

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{RCA}_0 + \mathsf{TT}^1$ prove $\mathsf{I}\Sigma^0_2$?
questions.context: The tree theorem for singletons TT¹ (every finite coloring of the full binary tree has a monochromatic subtree isomorphic to it) is a tree analogue of the infinite pigeonhole principle, which is equivalent to BΣ⁰₂ [@hirst1987]. Its first-order strength was a natural question since the obvious proofs use more induction.

questions.question: Is $\mathsf{SRT}^2_2$ or $\mathsf{RT}^2_2$ $\Pi^1_1$-conservative over $\mathsf{RCA}_0 + \mathsf{B}\Sigma^0_2$?
questions.answer: Yes for both. RCA₀ + RT²₂ is Π¹₁-conservative over RCA₀ + BΣ⁰₂ (Hwang 2026, an unrefereed preprint), hence so is SRT²₂, which follows from RT²₂. Earlier, RT²₂ + WKL₀ was shown ∀Π⁰₄-conservative over RCA₀ + BΣ⁰₂.
questions.context: RT²₂ implies BΣ⁰₂ and is Π¹₁-conservative over RCA₀ + IΣ⁰₂ [@cholakjockuschslaman2001], so the question is whether BΣ⁰₂ is exactly its first-order part. Le Houérou, Levy Patey and Yokoyama [@lehoueroupateyyokoyama2024] proved conservation for ∀Π⁰₄ sentences, which covers BΣ⁰₂ itself and the consistency statements usually considered.

questions.question: Does the thin set theorem $\mathsf{TS}^2$ imply $\mathsf{RRT}^2_2$?
questions.context: Both are consequences of RT²₂ obtained by weakening homogeneity [@cholaketal2005] [@csimamileti2009].

questions.question: Does the Ramsey-type 2-coloring principle $\mathsf{RCOLOR}_2$ imply $\mathsf{DNR}$? Does it imply $\mathsf{RWKL}$?
questions.context: Ramsey-type versions of graph coloring ask for an infinite set of vertices that can be monochromatic in some coloring. For k ≥ 3 colors they are all equivalent to RWKL [@bienvenupateyshafer2017], which implies DNR; the case of two colors behaves differently.

questions.question: Is there a $\Delta^0_2$ set such that every infinite subset of it or of its complement has a jump of PA degree relative to $\emptyset'$?
questions.answer: No — every Δ⁰₂ set has an infinite subset in it or its complement whose jump is not PA over ∅′.
questions.context: A set computes solutions to all computable instances of COH exactly when its jump is PA over ∅′ [@jockuschstephan1993]. A positive answer would therefore have shown that SRT²₂ implies COH in ω-models; the negative answer of Monin and Patey [@moninpatey2021] is the core of their separation of SRT²₂ from RT²₂ in ω-models.

questions.question: Does the Erdős–Moser theorem $\mathsf{EM}$ imply $\mathsf{COH}$? Does it imply $\mathsf{1}\text{-}\mathsf{GEN}$?
questions.context: EM and ADS together are equivalent to RT²₂ [@bovykinweiermann2017], and ADS implies COH. Since COH is the "unstable" part of RT²₂, whether EM alone already captures it is a natural question.

questions.question: Is $\mathsf{COH}$ generalized uniformly reducible to $\mathsf{SRT}^2_{<\infty}$? Is $\mathsf{COH}$ strongly computably reducible to $\mathsf{SRT}^2_k$ for $k > 2$, or to $\mathsf{SRT}^2_{<\infty}$?
questions.context: Dzhafarov [@dzhafarov2016] showed that COH is not strongly computably reducible to SRT²₂, a first step toward separating the two principles; these questions ask how far that separation extends.

questions.question: Is $\mathsf{WWKL}$ strongly computably reducible to $\mathsf{RT}^n_k$ for $n \ge 3$, or to $\mathsf{RT}$?
questions.context: Over ω-models, RTⁿₖ for n ≥ 3 is equivalent to ACA₀ and so implies WWKL. Strong computable reducibility forbids using the instance itself, and Hirschfeldt and Jockusch [@hirschfeldtjockusch2016] asked whether this matters.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{TS}^2$ imply $\mathsf{FS}^2$? Do $\mathsf{FS}^2$ or $\mathsf{TS}^2$ imply $\mathsf{EM}$?
questions.context: FS² implies TS² [@cholaketal2005]. Since RT²₂ ⇔ EM + ADS [@bovykinweiermann2017], comparing the free and thin set theorems with EM is a way to understand which part of RT²₂ they capture.

questions.question: Does the tree theorem for pairs $\mathsf{TT}^2_2$ imply $\mathsf{ACA}_0$? Does it admit cone avoidance?
questions.context: TT²₂ strengthens RT²₂ by coloring pairs of comparable nodes of the binary tree. Seetapun's cone avoidance argument for RT²₂ [@seetapunslaman1995] does not adapt directly because of the disjoint extension commitments of the tree structure.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{SRRT}^2_2 + \mathsf{COH}$ imply $\mathsf{RRT}^2_2$?
questions.context: The analogue for the rainbow Ramsey theorem of the decomposition RT²₂ ⇔ SRT²₂ + COH [@cholakjockuschslaman2001].

questions.question: Both $\mathsf{COH}$ and $\mathsf{EM}$ admit preservation of the arithmetic hierarchy.
questions.context: Wang [@wang2016] introduced preservation of the arithmetic hierarchy to separate principles by their definability strength, and showed that WKL and RRT²₂ have it. Patey [@patey2015d] proved the conjecture for COH and EM.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{2}\text{-}\mathsf{RWWKL}$ imply $\mathsf{B}\Sigma^0_2$?
questions.context: The Ramsey-type weak weak König's lemma relative to ∅′ is a consequence of 2-WWKL, which implies BΣ⁰₂ [@avigaddeanrute2012].

questions.question: Is the intermediate value theorem Weihrauch reducible to $\mathsf{RT}^2_2$?
questions.context: In the Weihrauch lattice, Ramsey's theorem for pairs cannot be reduced to PA, MLR or COH for reasons of Borel measurability [@brattkarakotoniaina2017], but which problems of analysis lie below it is less clear. IVT is a natural candidate: it is below WKL and computably true.

questions.question: How do the tree theorem $\mathsf{TT}^2_2$ and the Erdős–Rado theorem for the rationals $\mathsf{ER}^2_2$ compare? Does $\mathsf{ER}^2_2$ imply $\mathsf{ACA}_0$? Does $\mathsf{RT}^2_2$ imply $\mathsf{ER}^2_2$?
questions.context: Both strengthen RT²₂ by adding structure to the homogeneous set: a copy of the full binary tree for TT²₂, a dense subset of the rationals for ER²₂ (written η → (ℵ₀, η)² in some papers). Seetapun's argument fails for both because of "disjoint extension commitments" [@frittaionpatey2017]; Dzhafarov and Patey [@dzhafarovpatey2017] overcame it for TT²₂, while ER²₂ only has half of this difficulty yet remains unsettled.

questions.question: Does the Erdős–Rado theorem for singletons $\mathsf{ER}^1$ imply $\mathsf{I}\Sigma^0_2$?
questions.context: ER¹ (every finite coloring of the rationals has a dense monochromatic subset on some interval) and the tree theorem TT¹ have the same state of the art: both are provable in RCA₀ + IΣ⁰₂ and strictly stronger than BΣ⁰₂ [@frittaionpatey2017].

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{TT}^2_2$ imply $\mathsf{WKL}_0$? Does the stable tree theorem $\mathsf{STT}^2_2$ imply the cohesive one $\mathsf{CTT}^2_2$, or $\mathsf{COH}$, at least over ω-models? Does $\mathsf{SRT}^2_2$ imply $\mathsf{CTT}^2_2$ in ω-models?
questions.context: The tree theorem decomposes, like RT²₂, into stable and cohesive parts. These are tree analogues of the SRT²₂ vs. COH question; since SRT²₂ does not imply COH in ω-models [@moninpatey2021], the analogous question for trees is expected to have the same answer.

questions.question: Does the variable word theorem $\mathsf{VW}(2,2)$, or its ordered version $\mathsf{OVW}(2,2)$, imply $\mathsf{ACA}_0$? Are these principles provable in $\mathsf{ACA}_0$?
questions.context: Variable word theorems come from the Hales–Jewett theorem. Miller and Solomon [@millersolomon2004] showed that they are not provable in WKL₀, and noted that the classical proof of Carlson and Simpson goes beyond ACA₀. Liu and Patey [@liupatey2026] proved OVW in ACA₀ and showed that it does not imply ACA₀.

questions.question: Is the grouping principle $\mathsf{GP}^2_2$ $\Pi^1_1$-conservative over $\mathsf{RCA}_0 + \mathsf{B}\Sigma^0_2$? Does $\mathsf{EM}$ imply $\mathsf{GP}^2_2$?
questions.answer: First question, yes. WKL₀ + GP²₂ is Π¹₁-conservative over RCA₀ + BΣ⁰₂ (Le Houérou, Levy Patey and Yokoyama). Whether EM implies GP²₂ is still open.
questions.context: Patey and Yokoyama [@pateyyokoyama2018] introduced the grouping principle to obtain density bounds for the Erdős–Moser theorem in their conservation proof for RT²₂. Le Houérou, Levy Patey and Yokoyama [@lehoueroupateyyokoyama2024] later showed GP²₂ + WKL₀ Π¹₁-conservative over RCA₀ + BΣ⁰₂.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{RRT}^2_2$ imply Hindman's theorem for sums of exactly two elements $\mathsf{HT}^{=2}_2$?
questions.context: Csima, Dzhafarov, Hirschfeldt, Jockusch, Solomon and Westrick [@csimaetal2019] showed that HT^{=2}_2 is computably much weaker than full Hindman's theorem but still not computably true; the rainbow Ramsey theorem is a natural comparison point.

questions.question: Where does Cousin's lemma for Baire class 1 functions fall in the reverse mathematics hierarchy?
questions.answer: It is equivalent to ACA₀ over RCA₀.
questions.context: Cousin's lemma (every gauge on [0,1] has a fine tagged partition) is equivalent to Π¹₁-CA₀ for arbitrary functions coded suitably, and Barrett [@barrett2020] gave a heuristic suggesting the same for Baire class 1 gauges. The answer turned out to be much lower: ACA₀ [@barrettdowneygreenberg2021].

questions.question: Over $\mathsf{RCA}_0^*$, does $\mathsf{RT}^2_2 + \mathsf{I}\Sigma^0_1$ imply $\mathsf{B}\Sigma^0_2$?
questions.context: Over RCA₀, RT²₂ implies BΣ⁰₂ [@hirst1987]. Kołodziejczyk, Kowalik and Yokoyama [@koodziejczykkowalikyokoyama2020] studied Ramsey's theorem when only Δ⁰₁-induction is assumed, where RT²₂ alone does not even imply IΣ⁰₁; adding IΣ⁰₁ back is the natural intermediate case.

questions.question: Is $\mathsf{RT}^2_2$ computably reducible to the polarized Ramsey theorem $\mathsf{PT}^2_2$?
questions.context: PT²₂ is equivalent to RT²₂ over RCA₀ [@dzhafarovhirst2009], but the proof of RT²₂ from PT²₂ uses the principle more than once, so the question is whether a single application suffices.

questions.question: Is Hindman's theorem $\mathsf{HT}$ provable in $\mathsf{ACA}_0$? Does it imply $\mathsf{ACA}_0^+$? Is there a computable instance of $\mathsf{HT}$ all of whose solutions compute $\emptyset''$?
questions.context: Blass, Hirst and Simpson [@blasshirstsimpson1987] showed that Hindman's theorem is provable in ACA₀⁺ and implies ACA₀, and this gap has remained one of the most famous open problems of reverse mathematics. Every computable instance has a solution computable from ∅^{(ω+1)}, while some computable instance has no Δ⁰₂ solution [@blasshirstsimpson1987], improved to no Π⁰₃ solution by Liao [@liao2026]. A proof in ACA₀ would require solutions of bounded arithmetical complexity [@dzhafarovmummert2022].

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{RRT}^2_2$ imply $\mathsf{TAC}$?
questions.context: TAC, Conidis's tree antichain theorem (every infinite completely branching c.e. binary tree has an infinite antichain) [@dzhafarovmummert2022], follows from CAC and from 2-RAN; RRT²₂ and TAC are both principles strictly below ACA₀ that do not follow from WKL₀. Not to be confused with CAC for trees, which is TAC + BΣ⁰₂ [@cervellegaudelierpatey2022].

questions.question: Is $\mathsf{1}\text{-}\mathsf{GEN}$ Weihrauch reducible to the finite intersection principle $\mathsf{FIP}$?
questions.context: FIP is equivalent to 1-GEN over RCA₀ [@dzhafarovmummert2022]; the question asks whether the equivalence is uniform.

questions.question: Over $\mathsf{RCA}_0^*$, does $\mathsf{COH}$ imply $\mathsf{I}\Sigma^0_1$?
questions.context: Over RCA₀*, several consequences of RT²₂ such as RT²₂ itself, CAC and ADS do not imply IΣ⁰₁ [@fioricaroneskoodziejczykkowalik2021]. COH is the natural next candidate, since its usual proof iterates a construction along ℕ.

questions.question: Over $\mathsf{RCA}_0^*$, does $\mathsf{ADS}$ or $\mathsf{CAC}$ imply $\mathsf{CRT}^2_2$?
questions.context: Over RCA₀, ADS and CAC imply COH, hence CRT²₂, and BΣ⁰₂. Over RCA₀*, where only Δ⁰₁-induction is available, the usual proofs break down, and Kowalik [@kowalik2024] asked whether the implications survive.

questions.question: Over $\mathsf{RCA}_0^*$, is $\ell\text{-}\mathsf{CRT}^2_2$ equivalent to $\mathsf{CRT}^2_2$? Does it follow from $\mathsf{RT}^2_2$?
questions.context: The long version of a Ramseyan principle asks for a solution of cardinality ℕ rather than an unbounded one. Over RCA₀* some long principles (ℓ-RT²₂, ℓ-CAC, ℓ-ADS with set solutions) imply IΣ⁰₁, while ℓ-ADS with sequence solutions is equivalent to ADS; ℓ-CRT²₂ is equivalent to CRT²₂ over WKL₀* [@fioricaroneskoodziejczykkowalik2021]. Both parts would follow from a proof of the growing grouping principle GGP²₂ in RCA₀* + ¬IΣ⁰₁.

questions.question: Is $\mathsf{RCA}_0 + \mathsf{OVW}$ $\Pi^1_1$-conservative over $\mathsf{RCA}_0 + \mathsf{B}\Sigma^0_2$?
questions.context: Le Houérou and Patey [@lehoueroupatey2024] proved that the ordered variable word theorem, together with WKL₀, is ∀Π⁰₄-conservative over RCA₀ + BΣ⁰₂, by the largeness techniques developed for RT²₂. Patey [@patey2026] obtained full Π¹₁-conservation by formalizing a weakly low basis theorem for OVW.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{WKL}_0 + \mathsf{B}\Sigma^0_2$ prove the bounded Ramsey theorem $\mathsf{BRT}^2_2$? Does $\mathsf{CAC}$?
questions.context: BRT²₂ follows from RT²₂, from EM [@lehoueroupatey2025] and from IΣ⁰₂, but not from BΣ⁰₂ alone nor from ADS. These questions ask whether compactness, or the chain/antichain principle, suffices.

questions.question: Is $\mathsf{RCA}_0 + \mathsf{TT}^2_2$ $\Pi^1_1$-conservative over $\mathsf{RCA}_0 + \mathsf{B}\Sigma^0_2$?
questions.answer: TT²₂ + WKL₀ is ∀Π⁰₄-conservative over RCA₀ + BΣ⁰₂; full Π¹₁-conservation is open.
questions.context: The analogue for the tree theorem of the long-standing question whether RT²₂ is Π¹₁-conservative over RCA₀ + BΣ⁰₂.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{RRT}^2_2$ imply the finite intersection principle $\mathsf{FIP}$? Does $\mathsf{COH}$? Over ω-models?
questions.context: FIP is equivalent to 1-GEN over RCA₀ [@dzhafarovmummert2022], so the question asks whether these principles produce sets that are generic enough.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{ADS}$ imply $\mathsf{CAC}$?
questions.context: Hirschfeldt and Shore [@hirschfeldtshore2007] showed that CAC implies ADS and that both are strictly weaker than RT²₂. Lerman, Solomon and Towsner [@lermansolomontowsner2013] separated them with an ω-model built by an iterated forcing construction, a method that became a standard tool for separating Ramsey-type principles.

questions.question: Is the Erdős–Moser theorem $\mathsf{EM}$ strictly weaker than $\mathsf{RT}^2_2$?
questions.context: RT²₂ implies EM, and EM together with ADS (or CAC) implies RT²₂ [@bovykinweiermann2017]. Lerman, Solomon and Towsner [@lermansolomontowsner2013] showed that EM does not even imply SRT²₂.

questions.question: Is the tree theorem $\mathsf{TT}^2_2$ strictly stronger than $\mathsf{RT}^2_2$? Does $\mathsf{TT}^2_2$ prove $\mathsf{TT}^2_{<\infty}$, or $\mathsf{RT}^2_{<\infty}$?
questions.context: For singletons, the tree theorem is strictly stronger than the pigeonhole principle (Corduan, Groszek and Mileti). For pairs, a positive answer to the second question would make TT²₂ strictly stronger than RT²₂, since RT²₂ does not prove RT²_{<∞} [@cholakjockuschslaman2001].

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{SRT}^2_2$ imply $\mathsf{WKL}_0$, or at least $\mathsf{WWKL}_0$?
questions.context: Kjos-Hanssen raised the question in the Banff problem list as "a major problem in reverse mathematics", together with questions about subsets of random sets. Liu answered both parts negatively, even for RT²₂: RT²₂ admits PA avoidance [@liu2012] and avoids all closed sets of measure zero [@liu2015].

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{G}_\delta\text{-}\mathsf{REG}$ together with $\mathsf{WWKL}_0$ imply $\mathsf{RRT}^2_2$?
questions.context: Csima and Mileti [@csimamileti2009] showed that 2-randomness implies RRT²₂; the question asks whether weaker measure-theoretic principles suffice.

questions.question: The strong Tietze extension theorem (for functions with moduli of uniform continuity) is equivalent to $\mathsf{WKL}_0$ over $\mathsf{RCA}_0$.
questions.context: Giusto and Simpson [@giustosimpson2000] studied located sets in reverse mathematics and conjectured the equivalence; Shafer [@shafer2016] proved it for several versions of the theorem.

questions.question: How strong is the statement that if $\alpha$ is well-ordered and $Q$ is a wqo, then the $\alpha$-sequences over $Q$ with finite range form a wqo?
questions.answer: It is equivalent to ATR₀ over RCA₀.
questions.context: This is Nash-Williams' generalization of Higman's lemma to transfinite sequences with finite range. Montalbán expected the answer to come from an analysis of the maximal order types of the wqos involved. Pakhomov and Soldà [@pakhomovsolda2024] proved it in ATR₀, giving the equivalence.

questions.question: Is Nash-Williams' theorem — if $Q$ is a bqo, then so is the set of transfinite sequences over $Q$ — equivalent to $\mathsf{ATR}_0$?
questions.context: Marcone [@marcone1994] showed that the theorem is provable in Π¹₁-CA₀ but not equivalent to it, and Shore's work [@shore1993] shows that it implies ATR₀. Over ATR₀ it is equivalent to the generalized Higman theorem (if Q is a bqo, so is Q^{<ω}). The finite-range version for wqos is now known to be equivalent to ATR₀ [@pakhomovsolda2024], but the bqo version remains open.

questions.question: Is Fraïssé's conjecture (Laver's theorem: countable linear orders are well-quasi-ordered under embeddability) equivalent to $\mathsf{ATR}_0$? Is it even provable in $\Pi^1_1\text{-}\mathsf{CA}_0$?
questions.answer: It is provable in Π¹₁-CA₀, even in a weaker pseudo-Π¹₁-comprehension principle; whether it is equivalent to ATR₀ is open.
questions.context: Shore [@shore1993] showed that Fraïssé's conjecture implies ATR₀, and in fact that its restriction to well-orders is equivalent to ATR₀. Laver's proof uses bqo theory far beyond ATR₀. A negative answer would give a new robust subsystem of second-order arithmetic, since the conjecture is equivalent to many statements about the structure of linear orders under embeddability.

questions.question: Is there a system weaker than $\mathsf{ATR}_0$ that proves that the antichain $\mathbf{3}$ with three elements is a bqo? Does "$\mathbf{3}$ is a bqo" imply $\mathsf{ATR}_0$?
questions.context: RCA₀ proves that 2 is a bqo, and for every n ≥ 3 that if n is a bqo then so is n+1; but the only known proof that 3 is a bqo uses the clopen Ramsey theorem, equivalent to ATR₀. Freund [@freund2022b] made the first progress from below: "3 is a bqo" implies ACA₀⁺, and its Δ⁰₂ version implies ATR₀.

questions.question: Is the Auslander–Ellis theorem of topological dynamics equivalent to $\mathsf{ACA}_0$?
questions.context: Blass, Hirst and Simpson [@blasshirstsimpson1987] proved the theorem in ACA₀⁺, in the same paper as Hindman's theorem, and Simpson conjectured both to be equivalent to ACA₀. Kreuzer [@kreuzer2013] related it to minimal idempotent ultrafilters. The gap between ACA₀ and ACA₀⁺ remains open, as for Hindman's theorem.

questions.question: For all $2 \le k \le m$, the statement "every locally $k$-colorable graph is $m$-colorable" is equivalent to $\mathsf{WKL}_0$ over $\mathsf{RCA}_0$.
questions.context: A graph is locally k-colorable when each finite subgraph is k-colorable. By compactness it is then k-colorable, and Gasarch and Hirst [@gasarchhirst1994] showed that this is equivalent to WKL₀ for m = k. Their conjecture says that even the weak conclusion of m-colorability, for m much larger than k, already requires WKL₀. Schmerl [@schmerl2000] proved it.

questions.question: Is the problem of comparing well-orders by embeddings (WCWO) Weihrauch equivalent to unique choice on Baire space $\mathsf{UC}_{\mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}}$?
questions.context: Kihara, Marcone and Pauly [@kiharamarconepauly2020] looked for a Weihrauch counterpart of ATR₀ among the problems equivalent to it in reverse mathematics. Weak comparability of well-orders was one candidate; Goh [@goh2020b] showed that it is equivalent to UC_ℕ^ℕ, the problem of computing a path through a tree with exactly one path.

questions.question: Is $\mathsf{COH}$ omnisciently computably reducible to $\mathsf{RT}^1$, or to $\mathsf{D}^2_2$ or $\mathsf{D}^2_{<\infty}$?
questions.context: COH ≤_oc D²₂ means that for every COH instance there is a D²₂ instance all of whose solutions compute a solution to the COH instance, with no computability restriction on the D²₂ instance. Dzhafarov and Mummert [@dzhafarovmummert2022] call it "the distillation of the SRT²₂ vs. COH problem to its most combinatorial form". Monin and Patey [@moninpatey2021] separated SRT²₂ from COH in ω-models, which rules out computable reductions but not omniscient ones.

questions.question: Over $\mathsf{RCA}_0^*$, does $\mathsf{RT}^3_2$ imply $\mathsf{RT}^4_2$? More generally, does $\mathsf{RT}^n_2$ imply $\mathsf{RT}^{n+1}_2$ for some or all $n \ge 3$?
questions.context: Over RCA₀, RTⁿ₂ is equivalent to ACA₀ for every n ≥ 3 [@jockusch1972]. Over RCA₀*, where Σ⁰₁-induction may fail, Kołodziejczyk, Kowalik and Yokoyama [@koodziejczykkowalikyokoyama2020] studied what remains of this collapse when only Δ⁰₁-induction is available, and the question whether the hierarchy still collapses at exponent 3 remained open.

questions.question: Is $\mathsf{WKL}_0^* + \mathsf{CRT}^2_2$ $\forall\Pi^0_4$-conservative over $\mathsf{RCA}_0^*$? Does $\mathsf{CRT}^2_2$ imply that the cut $\mathrm{I}^0_1$ is closed under exponentiation? Is $\mathsf{RCA}_0^* + \mathsf{CRT}^2_2$ polynomially simulated by $\mathsf{RCA}_0^*$ for $\forall\Pi_3$ sentences?
questions.answer: CRT²₂ implies that I⁰₁ is closed under exponentiation over RCA₀*, hence it has non-elementary proof speedup over RCA₀* for Π₁ sentences (so no polynomial simulation); ∀Π⁰₄-conservation is open.
questions.context: Over RCA₀*, the cohesive Ramsey theorem CRT²₂ behaves very differently from RT²₂ and CAC [@fioricaroneskoodziejczykkowalik2021]. Kowalik [@kowalik2025] showed that WKL₀* + CAC is polynomially simulated by RCA₀* for ∀Π⁰₃ sentences, in contrast with RT²₂. Kołodziejczyk and Sun [@kolodziejczyksun2026] showed that CRT²₂ makes the cut I⁰₁ exponentially closed, which gives a large speedup and shows that CRT²₂ is not provable from CAC over RCA₀*.

questions.question: Is $\mathsf{RCA}_0 + \mathsf{BRT}^2_2$ $\Pi^1_1$-conservative over $\mathsf{RCA}_0 + \mathsf{B}\Sigma^0_2$?
questions.answer: Yes. BRT²₂ follows from RT²₂, which is Π¹₁-conservative over RCA₀ + BΣ⁰₂ (Hwang 2026, an unrefereed preprint).
questions.context: BRT²₂ follows from RT²₂ [@lehoueroupatey2025], so a negative answer would show that RT²₂ is not Π¹₁-conservative over RCA₀ + BΣ⁰₂ — the long-standing question on the first-order part of Ramsey's theorem for pairs.

questions.question: Is $\mathsf{RCA}_0 + \mathsf{HT}$ $\forall\Pi^0_3$-conservative over $\mathsf{ACA}_0$?
questions.context: Whether Hindman's theorem is provable in ACA₀ is open (see the question on Hindman's theorem). Le Houérou and Patey [@lehoueroupatey2026] suggest a weaker, first-order version of the question that the largeness techniques used for Ramsey's theorem might reach.

questions.question: Does the thin set theorem for pairs and three colors $\mathsf{TS}^2_3$ imply $\mathsf{EM}$? Does it imply $\mathsf{FS}^2$?
questions.context: TS²₂ is RT²₂, which implies EM, while Liu and Patey [@liupatey2022] showed that TS²₄ does not even imply the stable Erdős–Moser theorem, by preservation of 2-hyperimmunity. Three colors is the only case left. More generally, Cholak and Patey determined for which numbers of colors the thin set theorems admit cone avoidance [@dzhafarovmummert2022].

questions.question: Is $\mathsf{RT}^1_4$ Weihrauch reducible to $\mathsf{ADS}$?
questions.context: Over RCA₀, ADS implies RT¹_{<∞} since it implies BΣ⁰₂. In the Weihrauch degrees, Fiori-Carones, Shafer and Soldà [@fioricaronesshafersolda2022] showed that RT¹₃ is strongly Weihrauch reducible to ADC (and so to ADS) but RT¹₅ is not Weihrauch reducible to ADS: four colors is the remaining case.

questions.question: The generalized Higman theorem (if $Q$ is a bqo then so is $Q^{<\omega}$) is provable in $\mathsf{ATR}_0$.
questions.context: Marcone [@marcone1994] proved GHT in Π¹₁-CA₀ and conjectured that ATR₀ suffices, as a step towards his conjecture that Nash-Williams' theorem is provable in ATR₀: over ATR₀, the two statements are closely tied. Montalbán [@montalban2011] recalls that they are equivalent over ATR₀.

questions.question: Over $\mathsf{RCA}_0$, does Milliken's tree theorem for height 2, $\mathsf{MTT}^2$, imply $\mathsf{WKL}_0$?
questions.context: For heights n ≥ 3, Milliken's tree theorem is equivalent to ACA₀, and the full theorem to ACA₀′ [@dauriacetal2024]. Height 2 is the analogue of Ramsey's theorem for pairs, which does not imply WKL₀ [@liu2012]; the tree structure makes the usual separation techniques harder to apply.

questions.question: Is there a computable coloring of $\mathbb{N}$ with no $\Delta^0_4$ solution for Hindman's theorem?
questions.context: Blass, Hirst and Simpson [@blasshirstsimpson1987] built a computable coloring with no Δ⁰₂ solution, and Liao [@liao2026] one with no Π⁰₃ solution. A negative answer for some level n — every computable instance having a Δ⁰ₙ solution — is what a proof of Hindman's theorem in ACA₀ would require; a positive answer for every level would bring Hindman's theorem closer to ACA₀⁺.

questions.question: Does the maximal linear extension theorem for well partial orders imply $\mathsf{ATR}_0$ over $\mathsf{RCA}_0$?
questions.context: De Jongh and Parikh showed that every well partial order has a linear extension of maximal order type; the proof goes through in ATR₀. Montalbán studied the computability of such extensions. Marcone and Shore [@marconeshore2010] proved that the theorem is equivalent to ATR₀, as is the maximal chain theorem for well partial orders.

questions.question: Is $\mathsf{TT}^1$ $\Pi^1_1$-conservative over $\mathsf{RCA}_0 + \mathsf{B}\Sigma^0_2$? Is $\mathsf{RCA}_0 + \mathsf{TT}^1$ a $\Pi^0_3$-conservative extension of $\mathsf{I}\Sigma^0_1$?
questions.answer: Yes, TT¹ is Π¹₁-conservative over RCA₀ + BΣ⁰₂ (hence Π⁰₃-conservative over IΣ⁰₁, like BΣ⁰₂ itself).
questions.context: TT¹ is strictly stronger than BΣ⁰₂ (Corduan, Groszek and Mileti) and provable from IΣ⁰₂, and Chong, Li, Wang and Yang [@chongetal2020] showed that it does not imply IΣ⁰₂ in some models; the question was what its exact first-order part is.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{RT}^2_2$ imply the tree theorem for singletons $\mathsf{TT}^1$ over $\mathsf{RCA}_0$?
questions.context: In models of IΣ⁰₂ every instance of TT¹ has a solution computable from it, so the question only concerns models where Σ⁰₂-induction fails. Chong, Li, Wang and Yang [@chongetal2020] conjectured a negative answer.

questions.question: Does the tree theorem for pairs $\mathsf{TT}^2_2$ imply $\mathsf{I}\Sigma^0_2$?
questions.context: The analogue for trees of the result of Chong, Slaman and Yang that RT²₂ does not imply IΣ⁰₂ [@chongslamanyang2017]. Le Houérou and Patey [@lehoueroupatey2026] answered it by proving that a Carlson–Simpson lemma implying TT²₂ is ∀Π⁰₄-conservative over RCA₀ + BΣ⁰₂.

questions.question: Does $\mathsf{EXT}(\omega^*)$ (every countable well-founded partial order has a well-ordered linear extension) imply $\mathsf{ACA}_0$ over $\mathsf{RCA}_0$? What is its relationship with $\mathsf{RT}^2_2$?
questions.context: Downey, Hirschfeldt, Lempp and Solomon showed that EXT(ω*) is provable in ACA₀ and strictly stronger than WKL₀. Kierstead and Rosenstein showed that every well-founded computable partial order has a well-ordered computable linear extension, but Rosenstein and Statman built a computably well-founded one with no computably well-founded computable linear extension.

questions.question: Is the parallelization of $\Sigma^1_1\text{-}\mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}}$ strictly Weihrauch below $\mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}}$?
questions.context: Kihara, Marcone and Pauly showed that $\Sigma^1_1$-WKL lies strictly below the parallelization of $\Sigma^1_1$ choice on ℕ, which is below $\mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}}$. Anglès d'Auriac and Kihara separated $\Sigma^1_1$ countable choice from $\Sigma^1_1$ dependent choice, which gives the strict reduction.

questions.question: Does the weak infinite ray theorem $\mathsf{WIRT}$ imply $\mathsf{ACA}_0$ over $\mathsf{RCA}_0$?
questions.context: $\mathsf{ACA}_0$ proves WIRT (Theorem 7.5) and $\mathsf{RCA}_0$ does not, even for highly recursive graphs (Proposition 7.8), while the nonuniform version of WIRT is equivalent to $\mathsf{ACA}_0$ (Proposition 7.13).

questions.question: Is the hyperimmunity problem $\mathsf{HYP}$ strongly Weihrauch equivalent to the weak 1-genericity problem $1\text{-}\mathsf{WGEN}$?
questions.context: Brattka, Hendtlass and Kreuzer proved $\mathsf{HYP} \leq_{\mathrm{sW}} 1\text{-}\mathsf{WGEN}$ (Proposition 9.3) and $1\text{-}\mathsf{WGEN} \leq_{\mathrm{W}} \mathsf{HYP}$ (Proposition 9.4), so the two are Weihrauch equivalent.

questions.question: Does the Erdős–Moser theorem for infinitely many colors $\mathsf{EM}_\infty$ imply $\mathsf{ACA}_0$?
questions.context: ACA₀ proves EM_∞ through Ramsey's theorem for triples (Lemma 5.4 of [@towsneryokoyama2018]); for finitely many colors, fEM_{<∞} is Π¹₁-conservative over IΣ⁰₂ and so far from ACA₀.

questions.question: Does $\exists k \forall f\, \mathsf{DNR}(k, f)$, or $\forall f \exists k\, \mathsf{DNR}(k, f)$, imply $\mathsf{WWKL}$ over $\mathsf{RCA}_0$?
questions.context: For each fixed k ≥ 2, ∀f DNR(k, f) is equivalent to WKL₀. With IΣ⁰₂ the bounded versions also imply WKL₀ (Theorem 2.7 of [@doraishirstshafer2014]); with only BΣ⁰₂ they do not (Theorems 4.9 and 4.10).

questions.question: Does $\Sigma^1_1\text{-}\mathsf{AC}_0$ imply $\mathsf{ABW}_0$ over $\mathsf{RCA}_0$, without $\mathsf{I}\Sigma^1_1$?
questions.context: Friedman asserted the implication over RCA (full induction); Conidis proved it over RCA₀ + IΣ¹₁ (Theorem 2.1 of [@conidis2012]), and asked whether the implications of that theorem hold over RCA₀ — the other open one being ABW₀ → weak-Σ¹₁-AC₀. ABW₀ implies ACA₀ over RCA₀ + IΣ¹₁ (Lemma 2.2).

concepts.definition: For a set $X$ and $n, k \geq 1$, $[X]^n$ is the set of subsets of $X$ with exactly $n$ elements, and a $k$-coloring of $[X]^n$ is a map $c : [X]^n \to k$ (a finite coloring when $k$ is left unspecified).
A set $Y \subseteq X$ is homogeneous for $c : [X]^n \to k$ if $c$ is constant on $[Y]^n$; if this constant value is $i$, $Y$ is homogeneous with color $i$.
A coloring $c : [X]^2 \to k$ is stable if for every $x$ there is a color $i$, the limit color of $x$, such that $c(x, y) = i$ for all but finitely many $y$.
A set $L$ is limit homogeneous for $c : [X]^2 \to k$ if there is a color $i$ such that for every $x \in L$, $c(x, y) = i$ for all but finitely many $y \in L$.

A tuple $(H_0, \dots, H_{n-1})$ of sets is p-homogeneous for $c : [\omega]^n \to k$ if $c$ is constant on all $n$-element sets $\{x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}\}$ with $x_i \in H_i$, and increasing p-homogeneous if this holds when moreover $x_0 < \dots < x_{n-1}$.

A tree is a set $T \subseteq X^{<\omega}$ of finite sequences closed under initial segments. An (infinite) path through $T$ is a function $f : \omega \to X$ all of whose initial segments are in $T$; $[T]$ is the set of paths, and $T$ is well founded if it has no path. $T$ is finitely branching if every node has finitely many immediate extensions, and $b$-bounded if $\alpha(i) < b(i)$ for all $\alpha \in T$ and $i < |\alpha|$.
A binary tree $T$ has positive measure if $\lim_n |\{\sigma \in 2^n : \sigma \in T\}| / 2^n > 0$, that is, if the set of its paths has positive Lebesgue measure.

For a sequence of sets $R_0, R_1, \dots$, an infinite set $S$ is cohesive (for the sequence) if for every $i$, $S \subseteq^* R_i$ or $S \subseteq^* \overline{R_i}$, where $\subseteq^*$ is inclusion up to finitely many elements.
A function $f : \omega \to \omega$ is diagonally noncomputable (DNC) if $f(e) \neq \Phi_e(e)$ whenever $\Phi_e(e)$ is defined; relative to $X$, with $\Phi^X_e$ in place of $\Phi_e$.

A set $f$ has PA degree relative to $g$, written $f \gg g$, if every nonempty $\Pi^{0,g}_1$ class has an $f$-computable member (equivalently, every infinite $g$-computable binary tree has an $f$-computable path).
A set $S$ is hyperimmune if no computable function dominates its principal function $p_S$ (the function listing its elements in increasing order).
In a partial order $(P, \leq_P)$, a set $S$ is a chain if any two of its elements are comparable, and an antichain if any two distinct elements are incomparable.

In a linear order $(L, \leq_L)$, a set $S$ is an ascending sequence if $x \leq y$ implies $x \leq_L y$ for $x, y \in S$, and a descending sequence if $x \leq y$ implies $y \leq_L x$: a suborder of type $\omega$, resp. $\omega^*$.

A coloring $c : [\omega]^2 \to k$ is transitive if for every color $i$, $c(x, y) = c(y, z) = i$ implies $c(x, z) = i$. A 2-coloring of pairs is a tournament (who beats whom), and a transitive set is one on which the tournament is a linear order.

For a coloring $c : [X]^n \to Y$, a set $Z$ is thin for $c$ if $c$ restricted to $[Z]^n$ is not surjective, and free for $c$ if whenever $\vec{x} \in [Z]^n$ and $c(\vec{x}) \in Z$, then $c(\vec{x}) \in \vec{x}$.
A coloring $c : [\omega]^n \to \omega$ is $k$-bounded if each color is used at most $k$ times. A rainbow for $c$ is a set $R$ such that $c$ is injective on $[R]^n$.

A Martin-Löf test is a uniformly $\Sigma^0_1$ sequence of classes $U_n \subseteq 2^\omega$ with $\mu(U_n) \leq 2^{-n}$; a set is 1-random (Martin-Löf random) if it is not in $\bigcap_n U_n$ for any test, and $n$-random if it is 1-random relative to $\emptyset^{(n-1)}$.
The Turing jump of $g$ is the halting problem relative to $g$: $g' = \{e : \Phi^g_e(e)\downarrow\}$.

$\lim_y f(x, y) = z$ means that $f(x, y) = z$ for all sufficiently large $y$. By Shoenfield's limit lemma, a set is $\Delta^0_2$ exactly when it is $\lim_y f(x, y)$ for a computable $f : \omega^2 \to 2$ whose limits all exist.

A Turing ideal is a nonempty collection of sets closed downward under $\leq_T$ and under $\oplus$ (the ω-models of computability theory). As structures of second-order arithmetic, ω-models are those whose first-order part is the standard natural numbers and whose sets form a Turing ideal.

A partial order is well founded if it has no infinite descending sequence $x_0 >_P x_1 >_P \cdots$; a well ordering is a well-founded linear order. In second-order arithmetic, a countable well ordering codes a countable ordinal, its order type.

A quasi-order (reflexive and transitive relation) is a well quasi-order if it is well founded and has no infinite antichain; equivalently, for every sequence $(a_n)_n$ there are $m < n$ with $a_m \leq a_n$.
A sequence $(x_i)_i$ in a quasi-order $P$ is bad if $x_i \not\leq_P x_j$ for all $i < j$; a quasi-order is a well quasi-order exactly when it has no infinite bad sequence.

In a bipartite graph $G = (X, Y, E)$, a matching is a set of pairwise disjoint edges and a vertex covering is a set of vertices meeting every edge. A König covering is a pair $(C, M)$ of a covering and a matching with $C$ consisting of exactly one vertex from each edge of $M$.

A closed subset $A$ of a computable metric space $X$ is represented by negative information: a name of $A$ is a list of basic open balls whose union is $X \setminus A$. For $X = \mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$ the computably named sets are the $\Pi^0_1$ classes, and closed choice $\mathsf{C}_X$ takes its inputs in this form.

For a linear order $L$ with first element $0_L$ and a set $A$, a jump hierarchy on $L$ starting with $A$ is a sequence $\langle X_a \rangle_{a \in L}$ with $X_{0_L} = A$ and $X_b = (\bigoplus_{a <_L b} X_a)'$ for $b >_L 0_L$. Jump hierarchies on ill-founded orders were first studied by Harrison and are often called pseudohierarchies.

For a class $\Gamma$ of formulas of second-order arithmetic, the $\Gamma$ induction scheme $\mathsf{I}\Gamma$ consists of the universal closures of $(\varphi(0) \wedge \forall x\, [\varphi(x) \to \varphi(x+1)]) \to \forall x\, \varphi(x)$ for all $\varphi \in \Gamma$ (set parameters allowed).

For a class $\Gamma$ of formulas, the $\Gamma$ bounding (or collection) scheme $\mathsf{B}\Gamma$ consists of the sentences $\forall z\, [\forall x < z\, \exists y\, \varphi(x, y) \to \exists w\, \forall x < z\, \exists y < w\, \varphi(x, y)]$ for $\varphi \in \Gamma$: a bounded universal quantifier can be moved past an existential one.

A formula $\varphi$ is an atom of a theory $T$ if for every formula $\psi$ in the same free variables exactly one of $T \vdash \varphi \to \psi$ and $T \vdash \varphi \to \neg\psi$ holds; $T$ is atomic if for every $\psi$ consistent with $T$ there is an atom $\varphi$ with $T \vdash \varphi \to \psi$. A type of $T$ is principal if some formula consistent with $T$ implies all its members, and a model of $T$ is atomic if the only types it realizes are principal.

In an infinite partial order $P$, an element $x$ is small if $x \leq_P y$ for almost all $y$, large if $y \leq_P x$ for almost all $y$, and isolated if $x$ is incomparable with almost all $y$. $P$ is weakly stable if every element is small, large or isolated; stable if either every element is small or isolated, or every element is large or isolated. An infinite linear order is stable if every element is small or large (it has order type $\omega + \omega^*$).

A family $\vec X = \langle X_i : i \in \omega \rangle$ is nontrivial if some $X_i$ is nonempty; $\vec Y$ is a subfamily of $\vec X$ if every $Y_i$ is some $X_j$. $\vec Y$ has the $n$ intersection property if every $n$ of its members have nonempty intersection, and the finite intersection property if every nonempty finite set of its members has nonempty intersection. A subfamily with one of these properties is maximal if every subfamily with the same property containing it is contained in it.

A set $G$ is Cohen $n$-generic if for every $\Sigma^0_n$-definable set $W$ of finite binary strings, $G$ meets or avoids $W$: some initial segment of $G$ is in $W$, or some initial segment of $G$ has no extension in $W$ (relativized to $X$: $W$ is $\Sigma^0_n$ in $X$).

errata.correction: False for k = ℕ. The proof cites $\mathsf{C}'_k \equiv_W \mathsf{BWT}_k$, which holds only for finite k (Fact 2.1(1) of [@brattkarakotoniaina2017]). For k = ℕ, [[rt1n]] ≡W BWT_ℕ (Proposition 3.4 of [@brattkarakotoniaina2017]) and BWT_ℕ ≡sW K′_ℕ (Theorem 11.2 of [@brattkagherardimarcone2012]), which is strictly below C′_ℕ. The paper's own Lemma 7.31 (LPO′ ≰W RT¹_ℕ) agrees with the corrected statement.

Not for graphs with an arbitrary infinite vertex set, the paper's convention: [[wrsg]] and wRSgr are then cylinders (Proposition 7.2), while LLPO ≰sW RT²₂ (Corollary 3.15 of [@brattkarakotoniaina2017]). The strong reduction holds for graphs with vertex set ℕ, and the Weihrauch reductions hold; the results, about computable and Weihrauch reducibility, are not affected.

As in the journal version [@fioricaronesshafersolda2022]: false for graphs with an arbitrary infinite vertex set, for which [[wrsg]] is a cylinder, since LLPO ≰sW RT²₂ (Corollary 3.15 of [@brattkarakotoniaina2017]); only wRSg ≤W RT²₂ holds.
The sides are swapped: the proof (Lemma 3.7 applied to ATR₂ × ATR₂) and Theorem 3.10 give ATR₂ × ATR₂ ≰W ATR₂, so [[atr2]] is not idempotent.
